plan.summary:
Implementation plan for making MosaicPlan "much, much better": 7 waves, 33 work packages, ordered by user impact. The order is: (1) data safety and geometric correctness; (2) workspace safety UI, Android platform, honest colours, honest preview, photo intake and design system; (3) mosaic colour quality, live preview, freeform editor, face/detail guidance, viewer features, PDF foundations and project portability; (4) cut placement and accent colours, laying workbench, progress engine, PDF sheet structure, offline face detector; (5) undo/redo, single-pass stats, viewer back-buffer, PDF content, shopping view, target colours, PDF export UI; (6) deviation map and batch editing, fine-tile materials, colour measuring, streaming CSV, final PDF wiring; (7) docs and e2e consolidation.

RULES FOR EVERY PACKAGE

Files and parallel work
- Packages in the same wave run in parallel. They own disjoint existing files.
- New files may be created freely, but each name must be unique to its package.
- Some packages add optional fields or parameters only so that a package in the next wave can compile. Each one is marked "contract for wave N". Add them exactly as written, even if nothing in your package uses them.

Translations (i18n)
- Put new keys in src/i18n/ext/<package-id>.ts and export {de, en, tr}. The aggregator in src/i18n/index.ts merges every ext file after the base dictionaries.
- All three languages must have the same keys and the same placeholders. tests/i18n.test.ts checks this.
- To change the wording of an existing key, override it in your own ext file. First grep src/i18n/ext to make sure no other ext file already overrides that key.
- Never edit de.ts, en.ts or tr.ts.

CSS
- Only w2-design-system edits src/ui/styles.css.
- Every other package puts its CSS in src/ui/css/<package-id>.css and imports it from a component it owns.

Tests
- Unit tests go in tests/<package-id>*.test.ts.
- Browser checks are standalone Playwright scripts at e2e/<package-id>.e2e.cjs, run against `npm run preview`.
- Only w7-docs-e2e touches e2e/run-e2e.cjs and README.md.
- The golden mosaic hash fixture is tests/golden/mosaic-hashes.json. It hashes kind, c1, c2, rec, sub, line, free and palette hex+code, but not names. It is owned by whichever package owns src/core/mosaic.ts in that wave. Any change to it must be deliberate and explained in the PR.

Quality bar
- Every package must leave `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build` and the existing `node e2e/run-e2e.cjs` green.
- Every package must keep the exact-geometry and count guarantees: totals equal the geometry, and cut dimensions come only from analyzeCut on real polygons.
- Anything estimated must be labelled 'Schätzung' or 'Richtwert'. Requirement 18 holds everywhere.

packages.title: Reliable saving, atomic compute commit and mosaic integrity
packages.goal: No edit, rename or laid stone is lost on reload or tab close, and no failed save goes unnoticed. A compute that finishes in the background never corrupts the saved project and never brings a deleted project back. The saved record and the mosaic always belong together. The hook also provides the backup and manual-edit API that the wave-2 recompute guard needs.
steps: db.ts tx(): after the single request of a readwrite transaction, call t.commit() if it exists. Reset the cached dbp on db.onclose and db.onversionchange. If transaction() throws InvalidStateError, retry once with a new connection. Add a txMulti(stores, mode, fn) helper. Make deleteProject one transaction over all four stores.

db.ts: add optional fields to ProjectRecord: mosaicRev, imageRev, computedImageRev, meta.manualEdits. Add saveMosaicAndProgress(id, mosaic, progress), which writes both in one transaction over mosaics+progress. Add commitComputed(id, fields, mosaicWithRev, progress) as one readwrite transaction over projects, mosaics and progress. Inside request callbacks only (no other awaits), it reads the LATEST stored record. If the record is missing, abort and reject with Error('deleted'). Otherwise merge only the compute-owned fields (palette, diagnostics, computedWith, mosaicRev, computedImageRev, meta.computed/thumb/updatedAt, meta.manualEdits=0), then put the record, the mosaic and the progress.
serialize.ts: add an optional rev to StoredMosaic and keep it through pack/unpack.

src/core/integrity.ts: add maxColorIndex(data). It scans c1, plus c2 only for DIAG/LINE kinds, plus every sub array and free[].color. Add checkMosaicIntegrity(rec, stored) returning {ok, reason:'rev'|'index'|null}. Legacy data with no rev on either side passes the rev check.

useProject saving: change saveTimers to entries of {t, fn}. schedule() stores fn. flush() runs every pending fn plus every key in a failedKeys set via Promise.allSettled. The 'mosaic' job calls saveMosaicAndProgress, so progress is always saved together with the mosaic. Call flush on beforeunload, pagehide, and visibilitychange when hidden, each as flush().catch(()=>{}). Debounces become: rec 250 ms, progress 150 ms, mosaic 300 ms.

Save state: expose saveState ('saved'|'saving'|'error'), saveError {code:'quota'|'connection'|'other', message}, retrySave() (= flush), and exportCurrent(). exportCurrent returns a Blob built from IN-MEMORY rec, image and packMosaic(computed.data) through a new projects.ts buildProjectExport(rec, image, mosaic, progress). Refactor exportProject to use the same function. When a save fails, keep its key dirty and retry with backoff (2 s, 5 s, 15 s, 60 s).

compute(): use the snapshot r only to build the worker inputs. After the worker returns, set computedWith = computeKey(snapshot), or for custom mode computeKey of the snapshot with res.palette. Also set mosaicRev = uid() and computedImageRev = r.imageRev. Call await commitComputed(...). If it rejects with 'deleted', set computeError('deleted') and stop. On success, merge with setRec(prev => ({...prev, ...computeFields, meta:{...prev.meta,...}})); never spread the snapshot. Clear pending rec/mosaic/progress timers that belong to the replaced grid.

Loader: use a stored mosaic only when checkMosaicIntegrity passes. If it fails, set computed=null and expose integrityError = 'mismatch' so the UI can ask for a recompute. Never render a palette and grid that do not belong together.
Image identity: setPhoto sets imageRev = uid(). computeKey adds `im: r.imageRev` and omits it when undefined, so keys of legacy projects stay byte-identical.

Manual edits and backup: touchMosaic increments rec.meta.manualEdits. Expose manualEdits. Expose createBackupCopy(suffix): await flush(), then duplicateProject(id, suffix), returning the new id. duplicateProject copies the rev fields.
Bitmaps: release a replaced or unmounted ImageBitmap through a useEffect cleanup keyed on the bitmap. In the load effect, call bmp.close() when !alive.
acceptance: typecheck, test and build are green. tests/w1-persistence.test.ts covers maxColorIndex for all CellKinds, checkMosaicIntegrity for the rev and index cases, and checks that computeKey(rec without imageRev) equals the pre-change key string while setting imageRev changes it.
e2e reload: recolour J020, toggle 5 stones in lay mode and rename, then reload after 50 ms. All three changes persist.
e2e: rename and change the joint while a compute is running (city sample, 4 mm tiles). After the compute the name is still in IndexedDB and api.stale is true (stale badge visible).
e2e: leave during a compute, reopen, rename, reload. The stored palette.length equals maxColorIndex+1, and record.mosaicRev equals mosaic.rev.
e2e: delete the project during a compute. It does not reappear after the compute finishes and the page reloads.
e2e: change a laid stone's shape and navigate away immediately. After reopening, the stone's laid checkbox is unchecked.
e2e: patch IDBObjectStore.put to throw QuotaExceededError. No unhandled rejection occurs. After unpatching, the next edit plus a reload persists the earlier rename, because dirty keys are retried.
packages.risk: Effort L. This package changes the core save path. Keep the schema backward compatible: legacy records without rev must still load, so the index check is the only guard for them. Run the existing e2e flow before merging.

packages.title: Buildable cut pieces and honest cut instructions
packages.goal: Every planned cut piece is at least as wide as the user's minimum. Triangle edits are validated like line edits. Degenerate pieces can never produce Infinity values. Non-convex stones never get straight cut lines through their own body.
steps: geometry.ts: add convexHull (monotone chain), minCaliperWidth(poly) (minimum over edge normals of the max-min projection, skipping zero-length edges), and minInteriorAngle(poly).
pieces.ts pieceCuttable: only ever tighten. Keep the 2A/P >= min/2 test, AND require minCaliperWidth(isConvex(p) ? p : convexHull(p)) >= min - 1e-6. Do not add a hard rule on angle or edge length.

edits.ts setCellKind: for DIAG_A/DIAG_B, compute the two pieces with diagA/diagB(r, joint). Return 'diag-empty' when cleanPoly gives fewer than 3 points, and 'too-small' when pieceCuttable fails. For SUB, use subRects(...).every(pieceCuttable) in place of the hand-written min(sw,sh) test. Return early without touching progress when the kind and its parameters are unchanged.

edits.ts: export allowedCellKinds(layout, data, row, col, minPieceMm), a dry run of the same checks. Also export repairDegenerateCells(layout, data): number. It turns DIAG/LINE cells with a degenerate piece into FULL, keeps c1, and clears their progress. Wave 2 calls it on load.

pieces.ts analyzeCut: when cleanPoly has fewer than 3 points or the area is below 1e-6, return finite zeros with invalid:true, fits:false, needsCut:false, yieldPerRaw:1 and empty arrays. Add `invalid?: boolean` to CutInfo.

pieces.ts cutLinesFor: for non-convex pieces, split each edge's extended line into intervals at its polygon intersections. Classify each interval by whether its midpoint is strictly inside the piece. Keep the largest contiguous outside run that contains the edge midpoint. Return a parallel cutKinds: ('through'|'notch')[]. Convex output must stay identical. Prefer the placement with the fewest notch cuts.

StoneDialog: show notch cuts with their own text, e.g. 'Einschnitt i: von (x|y) bis Innenecke (x|y) – nicht durchritzen, ausknabbern/schleifen'. Show a 'cut.invalid' message for invalid pieces. Disable the Dreiecke, 2×2 and 3×3 buttons according to allowedCellKinds, with the reason as tooltip.
CutTemplateSvg: draw notch cuts as dotted orange lines. Add an advisory 'schwierig zu schneiden' badge when the minimum angle is below 25°. This is display only.

types.ts: change DEFAULT_SHAPES.minPieceMm from 1.5 to 2.0. In the ext file, override shapes.minPiece to 'Schmalste Stelle eines Schnittteils (mm)' and add a hint key. StepShapes: compute the sub-stone badge (line 29) with the same pieceCuttable(subRects) check, so the badge matches what compute does.
acceptance: Unit tests: pieceCuttable(1×5 rect, 1.5) is false; (1.5×5, 1.5) is true; the diagonal triangle of a 3 mm tile with 1 mm joint stays rejected at 1.5.
On all four samples with Home.tsx settings and DEFAULT_SHAPES, every piece of a DIAG, LINE or SUB cell has minCaliperWidth >= minPieceMm - 1e-6.

setCellKind DIAG on a 2×2 tile with 3 mm joint returns an error and the cell stays FULL. A 2×2 tile with 1 mm joint at min 1.5 gives 'too-small', the same as LINE at 45°. An 8×8 tile with 1 mm joint is accepted.
Clicking 'Ganzer Stein' on a laid FULL cell keeps its progress bit.
analyzeCut([]) returns only finite numbers and invalid:true.
For L, U and chevron fixtures, no sampled point on a cut segment lies strictly inside the piece. Rect, triangle and hexagon cut lines are identical to the old implementation.
With a 3×8 tile, 1 mm joint, k=2 and min 2, the StepShapes badge says no subdivision and compute produces 0 SUB cells.
packages.risk: Effort M-L. The stricter width rule changes automatic cut choices, so expect deliberate golden-hash updates by later mosaic owners. Do not touch freeform validation here; wave 3 handles it.

packages.title: 4x faster analysis loop, stable custom palettes, safe palette replacement
packages.goal: The analysis loop runs about 4x faster with bit-identical output. A palette the user built keeps every colour, its order and its codes through a compute. 'Palette aus Materialien' and colour removal can no longer silently scramble the stones.
steps: FIRST, before any change: write tests/w1-mosaic-core.test.ts. It computes the four samples (tests/helpers prepareFor, Home presets, seed 7) and hashes kind, c1, c2, rec, sub, line, free and palette hex+code. Store the hashes in tests/golden/mosaic-hashes.json.

Hot loop: replace mosaic.ts:217-219 `groupOf(() => 0, 1)[0]` with a scalar summation loop over SL/SA/SB, using the same formula and order. In the LINE search (mosaic.ts:327-330) set gA.n = cnt and gB.n = NS - cnt instead of reading counts from the Float64Array. Optional: monomorphic groupOf with an Int8Array of labels. Accept it only if the hashes stay identical.

Custom mode: add `code?: number` to FixedColor. When paletteMode === 'custom', skip the used-filter, the L* sort and the remap. Keep the input order. Set code = fixed[i].code when all codes are unique positive integers, otherwise i+1. Keep hex, name and materialId. Leave the other modes unchanged. Wave 2 passes p.code from useProject.

paletteOps.ts: add mergePaletteFromMaterials(palette, data|null, materials, formula) returning {palette, movedStones, maxDeltaE}. It appends missing materials with addPaletteColor and removes palette entries with no material counterpart through removePaletteColor in DESCENDING index order. Existing indices therefore stay valid and only removed colours are remapped.

StepColors 'Palette aus Materialien': when api.computed exists, use the merge, ask for confirmation first (stone count to be moved, max ΔE), then setPalette and touchMosaic. Otherwise keep the current replace.

StepColors remove(): show a confirm dialog with the stone count of the colour and the replacement colour code. Offer a choice of replacement through removePaletteColor's replacement argument. Mark palette rows with 0 stones as 'nicht verwendet'.
acceptance: Golden hashes are identical after the hot-loop change, i.e. bit-identical output.
A scratch tsx bench at about 1.2M cells shows analyze time at most 40 % of the old time. Note the result in the PR; it is not a CI test.

Custom palette of 8 colours with codes [1,2,3,5,6,7,8,9] and one colour no stone can use (pure yellow on the portrait): the result has 8 entries in input order with the same codes, yellow has 0 pieces, and per-colour counts match the old implementation by hex. A second compute with the returned palette gives the identical palette.

Merge test: compute custom mode from 12 materials, then merge with a reduced material list. The moved-stone count equals the stones of the removed colours, the total is unchanged, and every index is < palette.length.
Auto-mode outputs equal the golden fixture.
packages.risk: Effort M. Record the golden hashes before touching the code. Custom palettes stay correct across recompute only once wave 2 passes p.code through; until then codes become i+1, which is still stable for palettes without gaps.

packages.title: Correct raw-tile, pack, stock and cost totals
packages.goal: Raw-tile counts are never too low. Waste matches the displayed raw count. Packs and costs are counted per material, not per colour, so shared materials are no longer counted twice. Missing materials and invalid colour indices are reported instead of being silently skipped.
steps: Raw count: per colour, keep Map<CutInfo,count> and merge entries by a rotation-canonical key. The key is shape | rawW×rawH | yield | the polyInRaw vertices rounded to 0.1 mm and translated to the bbox origin, taking the smallest string over 0/90/180/270° rotations without mirroring. Memoise it in a WeakMap.

Set cs.raw = Σ ceil(n/yield) and cs.rawWithReserve = ceil(cs.raw·(1+reserve/100) - 1e-9). Keep rawExact as the lower bound. Compute rawArea = Σ cs.raw·rawW·rawH, so wasteArea and wastePct follow the rounded count.

perMaterial: { materialId, material, colors[], rawW, rawH, need (= Σ rawWithReserve of linked colours), stock?, toBuy?, packs?, packsToBuy?, cost? }.
- packs only when piecesPerPack > 0.
- toBuy when stock !== undefined; a stock of 0 counts as recorded.
- totalCost comes from perMaterial.
- costComplete is false whenever a colour with stones lacks a material, a pack size or a price.
- Colours without a material go into one 'ohne Material' group that uses the grid tile size.
Per-colour flags: materialMissing (materialId set but not found) and rawAssumedGrid.
invalidColorPieces: count pieces whose colour index is ≥ palette.length instead of skipping them with `continue`.

tests/core.test.ts: replace the tautological jointArea check (around line 261) with an independent invariant. For every cell, the sum of piece areas is ≤ the cell area. jointArea ≥ finishedArea minus the sum of cell areas.
acceptance: Strip plus diagonal triangle of the same colour on 8×8 tiles gives raw 2. One DIAG cell with both halves in one colour gives 1. Three isosceles diagonal triangles on 8×8 give 2. On 6×10, one DIAG_A cell with both halves blue plus one mirrored DIAG_B half in blue gives 2.
The existing 256-whole-stones test still gives 256/282.
Two colours share a material with piecesPerPack 100 and stock 50, needing 30+30: 1 pack (not 2), toBuy 10. Σ perMaterial.need equals rawWithReserveTotal.
wastePct is consistent with the displayed raw count. An out-of-range colour index is counted in invalidColorPieces.
typecheck and test are green.
packages.risk: Effort M. The raw count rises by 2-8 % compared with today. The UI already labels it an estimate; the README is updated in wave 7. StepPlan and the PDF still show per-colour packs until waves 3 and 5 switch to perMaterial.

packages.title: No ghost clicks, no accidental laying taps, correct German number input
packages.goal: A tap on touch screens can never tick 'verlegt' or switch to a neighbouring stone in the dialog it just opened. Taps at overview zoom no longer hit random stones. Typing '1.000' means 1000. The back gesture closes a dialog first.
steps: Viewer: set a tapHandled flag in onUp when a touch tap is recognised. Register a non-passive canvas 'touchend' listener that calls preventDefault when the flag is set and then resets it; reset it in onDown too. Give pointercancel its own handler that only clears state and never picks. Use a tap slop of 10 px for touch/pen and 5 px for mouse. Ignore presses longer than 500 ms.

Viewer small-target gate for touch/pen: compute the hit piece's bbox on screen (min(w,h)·scale). Below 28 CSS px, do not call onPick. Instead animate zoomAt(tap) until the piece is about 40 px (capped at maxS) and show a 1.5 s hint 'Zum Antippen hineingezoomt'. Mouse behaviour is unchanged.
components.tsx Modal backdrop: close only on a click where pointerdown also started on the backdrop.

components.tsx Modal history:
- On mount, call history.pushState({mpModal:id}, '').
- Guard against StrictMode double mount by checking history.state.
- A popstate that removes our entry closes the modal.
- ✕, Esc and the backdrop call history.back() when our entry is on top.
- A programmatic unmount pops our own entry.
- Keep a depth counter so nested modals close last-in-first-out.

numberParse.ts: add parseLocaleNum(s, lang).
- Strip spaces, NBSP and thin spaces.
- Grouping regex per language, with a leading [1-9] so '0.125' is not read as thousands.
- If exactly one '.' or ',' remains, treat it as the decimal point.
- Allow a trailing separator while typing.
- Validate strictly and return NaN otherwise.
NumberInput uses it in both places and shows a muted hint '→ 1000' (ungrouped) when grouping or spaces were removed.
acceptance: e2e at 390×844 with hasTouch on the computed portrait: 15 taps across the canvas at fit zoom open no dialog and toggle no stone, and placed-count stays 0 in the plan step. After zooming in, one tap opens the dialog and its stone-id equals the reference id; stone-placed stays unchecked.
e2e lay mode: a tap at fit zoom leaves placed-count unchanged and zooms in. After zooming, one tap changes placed-count by exactly 1. A 1.2 s long press changes nothing.
e2e: with the stone dialog open, page.goBack() closes only the dialog and the URL stays on /preview.
e2e: typing '1.000' in width-input (de, unit cm) shows '1000' after blur.
packages.risk: Effort M. preventDefault on touchend must not break pinch or pan; keep it limited to recognised taps. Modal history must not leave stale entries behind when Save closes the dialog programmatically.

packages.title: Robust material CSV import/export for German Excel
packages.goal: Material CSV from German Excel imports correctly. The app's own export round-trips. Re-importing updates materials instead of duplicating them. Every skipped or questionable row is explained. Deleting a material that projects use asks first.
steps: Move materialsToCsv and parseMaterialsCsv into the pure module src/core/materialsCsv.ts, with no UI or i18n imports.

Parser:
- Strip the BOM and honour an optional 'sep=X' first line.
- Pick the delimiter once from the header, counting outside quotes, in the order ';', tab, ','.
- Match headers case-insensitively after trimming and normalising umlauts and Turkish letters, against alias tables in de, en and tr.
- Map type words: Glas→glass, Keramik→ceramic, Smalten→smalti, Naturstein→stone, cam→glass, seramik→ceramic, anything else→'other' with a warning.
- If there is no HEX column, stop with an explicit error.

Numbers: with ';' or tab delimiters, accept ',' or '.' as the decimal mark. A value like '1.250' in an integer field is a warning, never a guess. Invalid or ≤0 sizes become a per-row warning or a skipped row. Return {items, updates, skipped:[{line,reason}], warnings:[{line,field,reason}]}.
Export: add an 'id' column and quote fields that contain the delimiter, a quote, CR or LF. Use ';' with decimal comma for de/tr and ',' for en. Use localized headers and keep the BOM.

Import preview dialog: 'N neu · M aktualisiert · K identisch · F fehlerhaft (Zeile 3: …)' with buttons Aktualisieren, Als neu hinzufügen, Abbrechen.
- Upsert by id first.
- Then match on normalised manufacturer+product+colorNumber+size, only when manufacturer and colorNumber are not empty.
- An update keeps the existing id.
- Nothing is written before the user confirms.
- Add a 'Vorlage herunterladen' button.
Before deleting a material, listProjects() and count the projects whose palette or settings.materialIds reference it, and name them in the confirm text.
await downloadBlob inside try/catch and show errors. Show the eyedropper hint (mats.colorHint) only when globalThis.EyeDropper exists; otherwise show a HEX-input hint.
acceptance: German Excel row with '12,50' and '9,5' parses as price 12.5 and size 9.5. Export→import round-trips losslessly in de and en, including commas, semicolons and quotes in text fields.
German, Turkish and capitalised headers import. A tab-delimited file imports. '1.250' in Stück/Packung gives a warning. An invalid HEX row is reported with its line number.
Re-importing the app's own export gives 0 new and N identical rows.
Deleting a material used by a project names that project in the confirm text (e2e).
packages.risk: Effort M. Updates must never change material ids, because project palettes link to materials by id.

waves.name: Wave 2 – Workspace safety UI, Android platform, honest colours & preview, photo intake, design system

packages.title: Safe recompute, save status, real step navigation and empty states
packages.goal: Recompute can no longer silently wipe laying progress or manual edits. Save failures are visible. Back and forward move between steps. Opening a project resumes where the user left off. Every step shows its status and what to do next.
steps:
Route-driven steps:
- Take the step from the initialStep prop when it is valid, otherwise 'photo'.
- User navigation (stepper, Zurück/Weiter, badges) pushes the hash, so browser back/forward and the Android back button move between steps.
- Capture the route step once in a ref. Only when the route had no step, redirect after load with replaceState: to 'plan' if placed > 0, otherwise to 'preview'.
onDone: setStep(cur => cur === 'compute' ? 'preview' : cur). If the user is on another step, show a 'Berechnung fertig – Vorschau öffnen' badge instead.

On every step change after the first, scrollTo(0). Centre the active stepper chip with stepper.scrollLeft, not scrollIntoView.
In w2-workspace-shell.css:
- Sticky stepper under the topbar for widths ≥ 601 px and heights ≥ 700 px.
- Sticky .step-nav at the bottom for widths ≤ 980 px, z-index 15, with env(safe-area-inset-bottom) padding and a centred 'Schritt n/10' counter.
- Put the step intro on the same line as the h2.

Stepper status:
- 'done' ✓ for photo when a bitmap exists, and for compute, preview and plan when computed && !stale.
- Warn dot when stale.
- aria-current on the active step.
- Steps 8-10 without a result get aria-disabled and a title, but stay clickable.

Empty states: Workspace renders EmptyState instead of the step component.
- preview, plan and pdf without a result: button that goes to step 7, or to step 1 if there is no photo.
- shapes and compute without a photo: button that goes to step 1.
- On step 1 without a photo, keep 'Weiter' enabled with the hint 'Foto kann auch später gewählt werden'.
- On step 7 without a current result, the primary button becomes 'Berechnen' and runs the guarded compute.

SaveStatus in ws-head shows 'Gespeichert ✓', 'Speichert…' or 'Nicht gespeichert'. On saveState 'error', show a role=alert banner with 'Erneut versuchen' (api.retrySave) and 'Sicherung herunterladen' (api.exportCurrent → downloadBlob). On api.integrityError, show 'Gespeichertes Mosaik passt nicht zur Palette – bitte neu berechnen'.

Recompute guard: if computed && (progress.total.placed > 0 || manualEdits > 0), open a Modal before computing. Text: '{placed} verlegte Steine und {edits} manuelle Änderungen gehen verloren'. Buttons:
- [Sicherungskopie anlegen und neu berechnen] (default): api.createBackupCopy('(vor Neuberechnung <Datum>)'), then compute, then show the name of the copy. If the backup fails, abort and offer exportCurrent.
- [Ohne Sicherung neu berechnen] in danger style.
- [Abbrechen].
Show compute.overwriteWarn as a warn line with the live counts.

Stale reasons:
- Diff the parsed rec.computedWith against computeKey(rec) by group: l = Größe/Steine/Fuge, a = Fotobearbeitung, rg = Bereiche, sh = Formen, pm/cc/cp/mi = Farben, di/de = Farbmischung, im = Foto ersetzt.
- Show 'Geändert seit letzter Berechnung: …'. The header badge reads 'Einstellungen geändert'.
- Add 'Änderungen verwerfen', which restores settings, adjust and regions from computedWith.

Diagnostics wording (ext overrides):
- 'Ø Farbabweichung je Stein (ΔE)' plus a rating word ('kaum sichtbar' < 2, 'erkennbar' 2-5, 'deutlich' > 5), shown only when deltaE is '2000'.
- deHint mentions that tile-size detail loss is not measured.
- Override compute.phase.lab to 'Farben umrechnen' and step.compute.intro.
acceptance: e2e: mark section A1 done and click recompute. The modal appears with 1.526 laid stones. Backup creates a copy in 'Meine Projekte' with placed-count 1.526. Abbrechen leaves progress unchanged.

e2e: going from colors to preview and then goBack shows step colors, and the active stepper button matches the hash. Reopening a computed project from 'Meine Projekte' lands on Vorschau, or on Verlegeplan once stones are laid.
e2e: a compute that finishes while the user is on step 'joint' leaves the step unchanged and shows the done badge.
e2e at 390×844: after each Weiter tap the step h2 is in the viewport, and .step.active lies within the stepper bounds.
e2e: steps 8-10 without a result show a button that leads to step 7.
e2e: with IDB put patched to throw, the alert banner appears. After unpatching, 'Erneut versuchen' persists the rename across a reload.
packages.risk: Effort M-L. pushState navigation must not reload the project; Workspace stays keyed by id. Test StrictMode double effects.

packages.title: APK saves visibly, back button, safe areas, WebView guard, crash recovery
packages.goal: In the APK the user always learns where a PDF, CSV or backup went, or that saving failed, and can share it again. The back button behaves like Android expects. System bars stay readable. Outdated WebViews get an explanation instead of a blank screen. A renderer crash reloads instead of killing the app.
steps:
platform.ts saveNative returns {savedPath:string|null, cacheUri, shared:boolean, error?:string}.
- Record Documents write errors instead of swallowing them.
- Treat a cancelled Share as shared=false, not as an error.
- Encode in chunks of 3 MiB, a multiple of 3 bytes. Call writeFile then appendFile into Cache, then Filesystem.copy to Documents/MosaicPlan, then stat and compare the size.
- Export timestampedName(base, ext) and reshare(cacheUri).

components.tsx: downloadBlob returns that SaveResult; on the web it returns {kind:'download'}. SaveResultNote (role=status) shows 'Gespeichert: Dokumente/MosaicPlan/<name>' ONLY when savedPath is set. Otherwise it shows a warning with the reason and a 'Teilen' button.
Projects.tsx: await export, duplicate and delete inside try/catch and show errors. On native, give backup files a timestamp in the name. Show SaveResultNote after export.

packages.title: Correct and unique colour names, exact colour matching, honest per-colour ΔE
packages.goal: Red is called red, every auto-generated name in a palette is unique, and names follow the UI language. The 'nearest colour' really is the nearest. The colours step shows how well each colour matches the photo and how many colours were actually used.
steps:
colorNames.ts:
- A curated table of about 50 reference colours {key, lab, de, en, tr}: reds/wine/carmine, terracotta, orange, ochre/yellow, beige/sand/cream, peach/apricot/salmon/skin light/medium/dark, browns, olive/greens, turquoise/petrol, light/sky/steel/royal/navy blue, violet/lilac/aubergine, magenta/pink/old rose, and greys.
- nameKeyFor(lab): achromatic branch when C* < 6, otherwise the minimum ΔE2000 reference.
- uniqueAutoNames(palette): among auto-named entries only, add hell/mittel/dunkel (light/medium/dark, açık/orta/koyu) for groups of 2-3 in L* order, then a running index.
- paletteDisplayName(p, lang).
- legacyDescribeColor: the old describeColor, kept for migration.

types.ts PaletteColor: add nameKey?, nameSuffix?, matchDeltaE?:{mean,max,over5,over10} and mergedFrom?.
mosaic.ts:
- Contract for wave 3: add FixedColor.stock?: number.
- Set nameKey on auto names and call uniqueAutoNames at the end.
- Accumulate per-palette stats from track(): source Lab vs assigned colour, remapped through keep.
- Set mergedFrom in auto-snap.
- Add diagnostics requestedColors and usedColors.

edits.ts:
- removePaletteColor picks the exact nearest remaining colour (brute-force ΔE).
- addPaletteColor de-duplicates auto names.
- updatePaletteColor: a hex change regenerates the name of an auto-named entry; an explicit name clears nameKey.
- Legacy migration: treat a name as auto only if it equals legacyDescribeColor(lab) in de, en or tr.

StepColors:
- In auto-snap and materials mode, show matchDeltaE (mean, max as tooltip, warn above 5) instead of the palette-vs-own-material ΔE, which is always 0.
- Notice: 'angefordert N – verwendet M (K Bildfarben zusammengelegt)'.
- Put Farbabstand and Farbmischung in <details className=advanced>. Open it when the values are not defaults; the summary shows the values.
- Override the mode labels in plain German: 'Automatisch aus dem Foto', 'Meine Steine – begrenzte Farbanzahl', 'Meine Steine – alle Farben', 'Eigene Farbauswahl'.
- A dangling materialId shows a disabled 'Material fehlt' option.
- Column order: Nr+swatch, Name, Steine, Bedarf, Material, HEX·L*a*b*, delete. Use nowrap CSS, and on phones (≤600 px) a reduced name-input width, in its own CSS file.
StepPreview legend: use paletteDisplayName, plus manufacturer and colour number as secondary text when a material is linked.
tests/core.test.ts: update the describeColor expectations. Golden hashes exclude names. If the exact matcher changes assignments, update the fixture and document the diff.
acceptance: Names: #FF0000 and #CC0000 → Rot; #8B0000 → Dunkelrot or Weinrot; #0000FF → Blau; #000080 → Marineblau or Dunkelblau; #FFFF00 → Gelb; #FFA500 → Orange; #808000 → Oliv. White and black unchanged.
Every reference key exists in de, en and tr.
Auto names are unique for the 4 samples at 16, 24 and 32 colours. Material names and user-typed names are never changed. A hex edit renames an auto entry but not a user entry.
nearestExact equals brute force on 100 % of seeded random palettes of 8, 12 and 16 colours. For 64 and 200 colours: under 0.5 % misses and worst extra ΔE under 1.
Removing #E5D149 from the landscape 64-colour palette remaps its stones to #FFF4C2.
Auto-snap test with a 336-colour gamut catalogue: matchDeltaE is populated, Σ counts equals the total pieces, and usedColors is below requestedColors with mergedFrom > 1 on merged entries.
packages.risk: Effort L. Changing the matcher may shift assignments slightly; take a deliberate golden update. Keep names short (about 22 characters) so the PDF legend still fits.

packages.title: Grout-aware honest preview and grout colour recommendation
packages.goal: The zoomed-out view, the PDF preview and thumbnails show what the wall will look like from a distance, including grout. Laid stones stay visible at any zoom. The joint step recommends the grout colour that gives the best effect from a distance and shows that estimated deviation.
steps:
buildOverviewRGBA(layout, data, palette, groutHex):
- Footprint per cell: fw = colW + g/2 on each inner side, same for fh.
- Covered area: colW·rowH for FULL cells, Σ area(cellPieces) otherwise.
- Mix: (Σ a·lin(c) + rest·lin(grout)) / max(A, covered), in linear light, using 256- and 4096-entry LUTs.
- Fix the doc comment.
- renderFull passes opt.groutHex ?? '#BDB8AE'. Viewer passes props.groutHex and adds it to the memo dependencies.

Overview path (pitch < 3 px): draw a second 1 px-per-cell overlay for progressMode (laid cells) and for focusColor dimming. In the detailed path, show laid stones with a desaturating grey-green tint instead of a white wash, and show the check mark from 6 px.
Viewer: read --viewer-bg once on mount and on theme change, not on every draw.

grout.ts:
- GROUT_CANDIDATES with generic names (Weiß #F2F0EA, Hellgrau/Beige #BDB8AE, Silbergrau #9A9A96, Zementgrau #808080, Dunkelgrau #5A5A5A, Anthrazit #404040, Schwarz #202020), plus the current colour.
- cellCoverage(layout, data?), computed per cell from the actual piece areas.
- perceivedDeltaE(targetLinPerCell, stoneLinPerCell|null, coverage, groutLin, sigmaCells=2): Gaussian blur over the cell grid in linear light, then mean and p95 ΔE00 against the blurred photo.
- recommendGrout(...): ranked results.

StepGeometry joint step:
- Compute the recommendation on the cropped photo downsampled to at most about 200k cells (reuse renderCropped read-only).
- Show 'Empfehlung: Dunkelgrau – Fernwirkung ΔE ≈ x (aktuell y) – Schätzung' with an 'Übernehmen' button. Never change the user's grout colour automatically.
- When a mosaic has been computed, also show 'Fernwirkung inkl. Fuge (Modell-Schätzung)' for the current grout, based on the computed stone colours.
- Add the hint that grout dries lighter, so the user should enter the HEX of a dried sample.
acceptance: recommendGrout on the portrait sample at default settings ranks a darker grout than #BDB8AE, with lower perceived ΔE. It does not force a dark grout on the animal sample.

e2e phone 390×844 with the landscape sample: zooming one step across the overview threshold changes the mean colour of the centre crop by ΔE76 < 3 (today 11.3). Changing the grout colour changes the overview pixels.
e2e lay mode at fit zoom: laid stones are visible in the overview.
packages.risk: Effort M. This only changes display and estimates; geometry and counts are untouched. The PDF picks up the new overview automatically through renderFull.
