packages.title: Robust photo loading, finger-friendly cropping, safe photo replacement
packages.goal: Huge or broken photos neither crash nor fail silently. Cropping works with a finger. Replacing a photo does not silently mismatch the old mosaic or old face regions. Custom palette codes stay stable across recomputes. Degenerate cut cells in old projects are repaired when the project loads.
steps:
imagePrep:
- readImageSize(blob): HTMLImageElement natural size, which already respects EXIF.
- loadWorkingBitmap(blob, maxPx=16e6): one uniform scale, orientation 'from-image', resizeQuality 'high'. Fall back to a full decode if the aspect ratio drifts by more than 0.5 % or the call throws.
- photoErrorKey(file, err) returns 'photo.err.heic', 'photo.err.decode' or 'photo.err.save'.

useProject:
- Use loadWorkingBitmap at both decode sites and keep sourceSize.
- In compute(): when the crop at the capped resolution has fewer source pixels than the target working size, decode a temporary full-resolution bitmap from image.original, render, and close it in finally.
- Custom mode: pass code: p.code into FixedColor.
- On load, call repairDegenerateCells (from wave 1). If it repairs any cells, expose repairedCells and schedule a mosaic save.

setPhoto(blob, name, {clearRegions}) sets imageRev (from wave 1) and clears regions when asked.
StepPhoto: when replacing a photo on a project that is computed or has regions, show a dialog:
- 'Neues Projekt mit diesem Foto anlegen' (recommended): createProject, then navigate.
- 'Foto in diesem Projekt ersetzen': regions are cleared by default; a checkbox keeps them.
- 'Abbrechen'.

StepPhoto:
- onFile is async with try/catch, a loading state and an error paragraph (role=alert). The previous photo stays when decoding fails.
- PhotoInput gets a primary?: boolean prop; 'Anderes Foto' is secondary.
- Show the original pixel size plus the working size when reduced.
- Add a dismissible tip 'Porträt? Gesicht in Schritt 6 markieren' (stored in localStorage inside try/catch).

CropEditor:
- Four corner handles, each a 44×44 transparent hit area with an 18-20 px dot, placed INSIDE the box so overflow:hidden cannot clip them.
- Resize around the opposite corner, projecting the drag onto the diagonal, with the aspect ratio fixed and clamped to the image.
- Minimum box size about 90 CSS px.
- setPointerCapture, plus pointercancel and lostpointercapture cleanup.
- A zoom slider (100-15 %) that scales around the centre.
- Readout 'Ausschnitt W×H px · ≈ N px pro Stein'.
acceptance: e2e at 390×844 with touch: dragging from 15 px inside the bottom-right corner by (-100,-100) shrinks the crop and keeps width/height equal to the layout aspect ±0.5 px. The same works from the top-left handle.
e2e: uploading an 8000×6000 JPEG shows the original size and a working size ≤16 MP, and the compute succeeds. An EXIF orientation 6 photo stays portrait with the correct corner at the top.
e2e: a corrupt file in the photo step shows the alert and keeps the previous photo.
Replacing the photo after compute opens the dialog. Choosing 'ersetzen' clears the regions and shows the stale badge.
Unit test: a custom palette with code gaps keeps its codes across two computes when run through useProject's input building. Test the helper as a pure function if needed.
packages.risk: Effort M. createImageBitmap resize options behave differently in older WebViews; keep the full-decode fallback. The memory peak during the first decode remains.

waves.name: Wave 3 – Mosaic colour quality, live preview, freeform, face guidance, viewer features, PDF foundations, portability

packages.title: Smoother colour gradients without stray colours, better 'own materials' palettes
packages.goal: The default output has smoother skin and sky gradients with no stones in an unrelated hue. 'Automatisch → eigene Materialien' really uses the requested number of materials and picks them well. Image colours the owned tiles cannot match are listed honestly.
steps: color.ts: add NearestColorMatcher.candidates(l, a, b, T=3). It returns up to 6 Euclidean-nearest allowed colours whose ΔE is within ΔE(nearest)+T, cached with the same quantised key as nearest().

mosaic.ts, FULL branch of Floyd-Steinberg: get the candidates from the cell's UNDITHERED analysed colour. Pick the candidate with the minimum ΔE to colour + error. Diffuse the residual exactly as today (7/5/3/1 split, ±25 clamp, scaled by the dither factor). Leave SUB, LINE and DIAG unchanged.

types.ts: set DEFAULT_SETTINGS.dither to 0.5. This affects new projects only. Override colors.ditherHint with the honest trade-off text ('weichere Verläufe, aber mehr Farbwechsel beim Legen; 0 % = einfarbige Flächen'). Override compute.meanDE to 'ΔE je Stein'.
Contract for wave 4: add ProjectSettings.pinnedColors?: {hex:string; name?:string}[] and ComputeParams.pinnedColors?: FixedColor[]. Both stay unused in this wave.

auto-snap: replace snap-and-merge.
- Summarise the weighted samples with kmeansLab at K' = min(256, n) and weight each centre.
- Precompute D[K'×materials] with params.deltaE.
- Seed with the snap set, then add greedily until k is reached or nothing adds gain.
- Run at most 2 FastPAM swap passes, with nearest/second-nearest caches and a 1.5 s cap.
- Cost is measured with the same matcher as the final assignment.
- Guard: keep the new set only if its cost is ≤ the snap set's cost.
- Deterministic for a given seed.
- Optional tie-break of -0.5 ΔE for FixedColor.stock > 0, applied in selection only.

Missing colours: in auto-snap, centres whose nearest material is more than ΔE 5 away go into diagnostics.missingColors {hex, lab, stones, nearestMaterialId, deltaE}. Count stones exactly with a nearest-centre pass in the assignment loop. StepColors shows them in a panel 'Fehlende Farben – Farbton zum Nachkaufen (Zielwert)'. Never name a product.
acceptance: Dither 0 vs 1 on the portrait sample: data.kind is identical, and stats pieces, gridPositions and the per-colour sum are identical.
At dither 1, stones whose colour is more than 5 ΔE worse than the nearest palette colour number at most the dither-0 count plus 1 % of stones.
Perceived ΔE (blur σ = 1 cell, linear light) at 0.5 is ≤ the value at 0 on all 4 samples.
Scratch bench at 2M cells, 200 colours: the assign phase at dither 0.5 is faster than today's 11 s. Report the number.
Golden fixture updated deliberately, with the diff explained.
packages.risk: Effort M-L. Changing the default dither changes the look of new projects; the hint states the trade-off. The selection must be bounded in time for large material DBs.

packages.title: Live mosaic preview in steps 2-6, instant 'Übernehmen', compute that survives navigation
packages.goal: While choosing size, tiles, joint, colours and shapes, the user sees the mosaic update live, and nothing is saved until they commit. A compute keeps running and stays visible when the user leaves and reopens the project.
steps: client.ts: add 'preview' to the Channel type. Cancelling with cancelChannel('preview') never affects compute or PDF jobs.

useProject:
- Factor prepareInputs(r) (crop, working size, renderCropped, canvasToRaw, fixed palette incl. stock: m.stock), with the raw image cached by {adjust, crop, ws, imageRev}.
- runCompute(r, channel) → {key, lang, materialsSig, ws, layout, layoutParams, data, palette, diagnostics, processed}.
- commit(result) = the wave-1 commitComputed path.

Preview state:
- On computeKey change, debounce (about 500 ms for chips, 800 ms for typed numbers), call cancelChannel('preview'), and use a request counter so stale results are dropped.
- Run automatically only while cells ≤ 60k (≤ 30k when hardwareConcurrency ≤ 4 or the pointer is coarse) and the last preview took < 1.5 s. Otherwise show a 'Vorschau aktualisieren' button with an estimated time.
- The preview never writes to IndexedDB, rec.palette, computedWith or progress.

jobs.ts registry, Map<projectId, {progress, promise, cancel}> plus subscribe:
- startCompute moves the worker call and the commit out of the component.
- useProject subscribes on mount, so a reopened project shows the phase, progress and Cancel button and adopts the result when it resolves.
- Only one compute runs app-wide. Other projects show 'Berechnung für „X“ läuft noch' with Abbrechen.
Contract for wave 4: touchProgress(dirtyCells?: number[]) and touchMosaic(dirtyCells?: number[]) accept an optional parameter that is ignored for now.

LivePreview:
- renderFull at about 640 px with groutHex, surface and realistic.
- A permanent badge 'Vorschau – noch nicht übernommen'.
- The old image is dimmed with a spinner while updating.
- Photo/mosaic toggle.
- A compact stat strip with exact geometry values only; no per-colour counts.
- Workspace mounts it for steps size, tiles, joint, colors and shapes: as a right-hand panel on desktop, sticky at about 35vh above the controls at ≤980 px, and collapsible on the shapes step so the region editor stays usable.

StepCompute becomes 'Übernehmen / Berechnen':
- If preview.key, lang, materials and ws match, commit the preview directly with no second compute.
- The wave-2 recompute guard still applies.
- Auto-commit on entering the preview step only when nothing has been computed yet.
- Show diagnostics.usedColors/requestedColors in the summary.
acceptance: Vitest: for the 4 samples, runCompute output for a key equals the committed output byte for byte (packMosaic, fixed seed).
e2e: in step tiles a canvas appears and changes when switching 4→8 mm. computedWith in IndexedDB stays unchanged until 'Übernehmen'.
e2e: on a project with laid stones, visiting steps 2-6 keeps progress-pct unchanged.
e2e: after a matching preview, 'Übernehmen' finishes in under 300 ms and posts no second compute message (Worker.postMessage counted via an init script).
e2e: leaving during a compute and reopening shows the progress bar and Cancel. Starting a compute in another project shows the 'läuft noch' message.
packages.risk: Effort L. Preview and commit must use one shared pipeline so that what the user sees is exactly what is saved. Test that the job registry keeps working after a reload.

packages.title: Reliable freeform validation and a usable contour editor
packages.goal: Freeform stones can no longer overlap or silently lose their joint. Errors are explained in the user's language and point to the affected piece. Drawing a custom cut stone is practical on desktop and touch.
steps:
geometry.ts:
- triangulate(poly): ear clipping on the cleaned polygon, made CCW first.
- polygonIntersectionArea(a,b): sum over triangle pairs, clipping each by the other's half-planes with clipHalfPlane.
- polygonDistance(a,b): 0 when edges intersect (including collinear or touching) or a vertex lies inside the other polygon; otherwise the minimum vertex-to-segment distance.

edits.ts validateFreePieces(cellW, cellH, pieces, minPieceMm, joint):
- Return typed issues: noPieces, tooMany{max}, tooFewPoints{piece}, selfIntersect{piece}, outside{piece}, areaTooSmall{piece}, overlap{a,b} when the intersection area is > 0.01 mm², thin{piece,minMm}.
- When joint > 0 and the gap is < joint - 0.01 mm, add a gap{a,b,gapMm} WARNING (not an error).
- setFreePieces passes layout.joint.
pieces.ts: add freePreset(kind, w, h, joint) for full, diagonal ╲, diagonal ╱, half, rhombus and trapezoid. Build them on diagA, diagB, lineSplit and subRects so they include the joint.

FreeformEditor:
- SVG viewBox in mm, width min(560px, 100%), max-height 60vh. Convert pointer positions with getScreenCTM().inverse().
- Draggable vertices: setPointerCapture, touch-action:none, snap to cell edges within 0.2 mm, no extra point added after a drag.
- Click an edge midpoint to insert a vertex; each vertex row has a delete control.
- 'Neu zeichnen' button and preset buttons.
- Stop rounding the pre-filled pieces; round only clicked or dragged points to 0.1 mm.
- Live edge lengths, a dashed closing segment, and the active piece's area.
- Pieces with issues get a red dashed outline. Issues are translated, one per line, e.g. 'Teil 1 und Teil 3 überlappen sich'. A reason is shown next to the disabled Speichern button.

StoneDialog:
- Show a badge 'Material fehlt (gelöscht oder nicht importiert)' instead of '?'.
- Use paletteDisplayName for colour names.
- Override edit.lineHint with explicit directions: 0° = senkrecht, 45° = ╱, 90° = waagerecht, 135° = ╲, offset in mm.
acceptance: Unit tests: two 8×5 strips overlapping in an 8×8 cell are rejected. The stacked pair [[3.5,4],[5.5,4],[5.5,7.5],[3.5,7.5]] / [[3.5,1.5],[5.5,1.5],[5.5,5.5],[3.5,5.5]] is rejected. Two triangles sharing a diagonal with a 1 mm gap are accepted. Touching pieces give a gap warning, not an error.
Round trip: every DIAG, SUB and LINE cell opened in the editor validates with no errors and no gap warnings, across 6 tile sizes and joints of 0.5-3 mm. Every freePreset validates.
e2e: on a diagonal cell, 'Neu zeichnen', draw a triangle, drag one vertex (its table coordinates change), save. The stone count and cut template reflect the new piece.
packages.risk: Effort M-L. Gap is a warning so that existing saved projects still open. Keep the exact cut dimensions coming from analyzeCut.

packages.title: Face resolution guidance, detail meter, safe region drawing, translated layout errors
packages.goal: Before computing, the user learns whether a face will be recognisable (stones across the face), sees exact trade-offs, and can apply them with one click. Region drawing no longer steals scroll gestures. Layout errors appear in the UI language.
steps:
layout.ts:
- regionCellSpan(layout, region) → {cols, rows, mmW, mmH}, counting cells whose centres lie in the region (centre row and column for ellipses), using colX/colW and rowY/rowH.
- class LayoutError extends Error {code: 'invalidDims'|'smallerThanTile'|'tooManyCells'; params}, keeping the German message as fallback.
- parseCellId: change the suffix group to `-([1-9]\d*)`.

StepGeometry LayoutSummary:
- Call computeLayout locally inside try/catch. If it throws a LayoutError, render t(`layout.err.${code}`) with numbers formatted by n(), plus an action hint.
- Add a 'Detailgrad (Richtwert)' block. When face regions exist, show 'Gesicht ≈ N × M Steine' with a traffic light (red < 16, yellow 16-29, green ≥ 30) and the reason. Without face regions, show a neutral pointer to step 6.

Tiles step honesty: next to tiles.mixedHint add an 'unvollständig' badge reading 'nur als 2×2/3×3-Teilung einer Rasterzelle; Zonen mit eigenem Raster fehlen noch', and show the computed sub-stone size in mm.

Move RegionEditor from StepShapes into RegionEditor.tsx.
- Add a 'Bereich zeichnen' toggle (aria-pressed). Default touch-action is pan-y pinch-zoom; drawing mode uses none.
- Touch input only draws when the toggle is on; mouse and pen always draw.
- Handle pointercancel and lostpointercapture without saving the draft.
- Minimum region size 24 px on screen. The toggle turns off after one region is drawn.
- Show number labels on the regions, 44 px delete buttons and 'Letzten Bereich entfernen'.
- Show the face span readout per face region.
- Hide 'Gesichter erkennen' when FaceDetector is missing, and instead show a card prompting the user to mark the face by hand.
- Show 'Bereiche geändert – bitte neu berechnen' when the mosaic has been computed.
acceptance: Unit tests: regionCellSpan with 300×400 mm, 8 mm tiles, 1 mm joint and region w=0.46 gives 15 across; with 400 mm and 5 mm tiles it gives 31. parseCellId('A001-0') is null and 'A001-2' gives piece 1. computeLayout throws LayoutError with the correct codes.
e2e with EN UI: width 0.1 cm shows the English layout error.

e2e at 390×844 touch: a vertical swipe on the region image with drawing off scrolls the page and leaves the region count unchanged. With drawing on, one drag adds exactly one region and the toggle turns off.
e2e: 'Übernehmen' on a trade-off row updates grid positions to the computeLayout value. In Chromium the detect button is absent and the manual-marking card is visible.
packages.risk: Effort M-L. Thresholds must be labelled 'Richtwert'. Applying suggestions only changes settings; the recompute guard protects existing progress.

packages.title: Rulers, section focus, paint/rectangle modes and photo comparison in the viewer
packages.goal: The viewer has row/column rulers that match the stone IDs and the PDF. It can dim everything outside a section or colour. It supports brush and rectangle selection, long-press and hover inspection, and an exact photo-vs-mosaic comparison slider.
steps:
render.ts:
- RenderOptions.rulers: an 18 px top and left band with col+1 and rowLabel(row) for the visible range. Use the same label-skipping rule as the PDF labelStep (every label at ≥14 px, then every 5th or 10th). Highlight the selected row and column.
- focusRange: a semi-opaque overlay outside the range in both the detailed and the overview path.
- focusColor dims other colours with a grey wash, so they cannot be confused with the laid-stone tint.

Viewer props:
- focusRange plus onOutsideTap(section hint): taps outside the range never pick.
- mode 'tap' | 'paint' | 'rect':
  - paint: one-pointer drag calls onPaint({idx,piece}[], set) with the target state taken from the first piece;
  - rect: drag a cell-snapped rectangle and call onRect(range);
  - in both modes, two fingers, Space or the middle mouse button pan; the cursor is a crosshair.
- onLongPick(row, col, piece) after 500 ms.
- flash?: {idx, piece} for about 600 ms.
- On desktop, a hover status line with pieceId and X/Y in mm.

Viewer comparison: compareImage?: CanvasImageSource and compareSplit?: number. After renderMosaic, draw the image clipped into the world rectangle (0, 0, finishedW, finishedH) with the same transform, plus a handle line. The image lines up exactly because the photo is sampled on that rectangle.
Viewer height: at ≥981 px use clamp(420px, calc(100dvh - 200px), 1100px); keep 62vh below that.

StepPreview:
- Turn rulers on.
- Add a 'Vergleich Foto/Mosaik' toggle with a range slider and a press-and-hold 'Foto zeigen' button, using api.processed.
- Move the processed-photo thumbnail above the legend.
- Show 'originalAfterCompute' only when nothing has been computed; when computed but no reference is in memory, show 'Referenz nach Neuladen nicht verfügbar – wird in Kürze gespeichert'. Wave 5 persists the reference.
acceptance: Unit tests for the pure helpers: label step and visible label indices for several pitches; ruler labels equal cellId row/col parts; focus-overlay rectangles cover exactly the outside area.
Existing e2e/run-e2e.cjs and e2e/w1-touch-input-safety.e2e.cjs still pass.
e2e preview: rulers show 'A' and '1' at fit zoom. The comparison slider at 50 % shows photo pixels on the left half: the canvas pixel at 25 % width matches the processed image within 10 RGB levels.
packages.risk: Effort M-L. The new modes must not change default tap behaviour. Consumers in StepPlan are wired up in wave 4.

packages.title: Readable tables, correct labels, honest truncation, bookmarks and print-at-100 %
packages.goal: No text overlaps in tables or key/value blocks. Join labels and column numbers stay off the stones. Coordinate lists say when they are cut off. Fit-to-page uses one standard scale. The PDF has bookmarks, a page column, links and PrintScaling=None. Shared materials are costed correctly. A corrupted palette mapping can never be printed.
steps:
pdfTable.ts: a pure layoutTable(columns:{min, wrap?}[], rows, measure, avail) plus a drawTable wrapper.
- Columns that must not wrap (codes, HEX, numbers, sizes) are sized to their widest cell.
- Text columns share the rest and wrap at spaces or hyphens only.
- Widths only shrink, never stretch; then the font steps down to 7 and 6.5 pt.
- Never ellipsize or split an identifier.
- Multi-line rows have their own height; the page-break test uses that height.
- Wrapped header band.
- Replace table() in pdf.ts with it.

Key/value blocks on the cover, section cover and material summary: label width = max measured label + 3 mm, wrapped. The section cover moves the mini-map below the block when the page is narrower than 140 mm. The legend gets separate Material and Farbnr. columns.

Page numbers at baseline PH-6.5. Laying-sheet footers read 'Blatt A1-1 · Seite 9 / 74'. Add a rotText helper that never passes align or baseline together with angle. Use it for the right-edge join label (inside the margin, vertically centred, moved to sideInfo if too long) and for rotated column numbers.

Coordinate list: set truncated exactly where a piece is skipped, using a labelled outer loop. The per-section title reads 'erste N von M Steinen – Rest siehe CSV' or 'vollständig'. Print the notice directly under the last table. Use one cellPieces-based count.

pdfOptions.ts: add fitSheetScale(allSections, printW, printH). It takes the minimum over ALL sections and snaps DOWN to a standard series (4, 3, 2, 1, 1/1.25, 1/1.5, 1/2, 1/2.5, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5, …, 1/100). Add sheetPrintArea(PW, PH) and fmtScale ('1:1,5'). Use them everywhere, including the cover.

doc.setProperties({title: 'MosaicPlan – <name>'}) and viewerPreferences({PrintScaling:'None', DisplayDocTitle:true}). Record page numbers while generating and build an outline: chapters, then sections, then sheets. Use raw Unicode titles, not safe(). Add a 'Seite' column to the overview section table, filled in afterwards, with doc.link rows and links on the overview map. Add links on the section mini-map boxes.
Material list: use stats.perMaterial (packs, toBuy, cost per material, 'ohne Material' group, missing-material marks). Use paletteDisplayName for colour names.
Guard: if stats.invalidColorPieces > 0 or maxColorIndex ≥ palette.length (src/core/integrity.ts), throw a translated error instead of drawing.
acceptance: Unit test of layoutTable boxes: no two boxes intersect and all lie within [M, PW-M], for de and tr with 40-character material names and 'VT-1000-GLOSS' colour numbers, on A4 and on 120×297 mm. Each colour number stays one token.
Coordinate notice: present for a single section with coordLimit = pieces-1; present for a multi-section project with the limit inside the last section; absent when coordLimit ≥ pieces.
Output contains /Outlines, /PrintScaling /None and /Title. Each section's outline entry points to a page whose header contains 'Abschnitt <id>'.
Fit mode: 600×800 mm on A4 shows a single scale string on all sheets; 500×700 mm on A3 landscape snaps to 1:1.
The existing PDF==preview per-colour fill test still passes. A tampered palette index makes generatePdf reject.
packages.risk: Effort L. Many small layout changes in one file; run the pdftotext overlap check from the audit before merging. The page count may change slightly.

packages.title: Project export/import carries its materials
packages.goal: Moving a project between devices keeps its material links, raw sizes and costs. Importing never overwrites local materials, and the result is reported.
steps: Export payload version 2 adds `materials`: only those referenced by palette[].materialId or a non-empty settings.materialIds.

materialImport.ts: pure planMaterialImport(exported, local) → {mapping, inserts, notes}.
- If a local material has the same id, keep the local one and note any differences.
- Otherwise match exactly on normalised manufacturer+product+colorNumber+size.
- Otherwise insert with the original id.
- Never pick a 'nearest' material.

importProject: apply the plan and remap palette materialIds and settings.materialIds before saving. Append ' (Import)' when a project with the same name exists. For version 1 files, warn 'Datei enthält keine Materialien – N Farben ohne gültiges Material'. Return the summary.
Projects.tsx: show 'X Materialien neu angelegt, Y vorhandenen zugeordnet, Z mit abweichenden Daten' after import.
acceptance: Unit tests for planMaterialImport: empty local store; conflicting id with different data (local kept, note produced); exact-match remap; no 'nearest' matching.
e2e: export in context A, import in a fresh context B. StoneDialog shows the material name (not 'Material fehlt'), and 'Rohsteine inkl. Reserve' equals the value in context A.
packages.risk: Effort S-M. Keep version 1 imports working.

waves.name: Wave 4 – Cut placement & accents, laying workbench, progress engine, PDF sheet structure, offline face detection

packages.title: Cuts where they matter, colours the face needs, optional continuous contours
packages.goal: The user can focus cutting work on marked faces and details. Small but essential colours such as pupils can be detected and pinned. Contour cuts can optionally line up across neighbouring stones. Diagnostics show where the cuts went.
steps: types.ts ShapeOptions: add bgCutFactor?: number (undefined means 1) and contourContinuity?: boolean (default false). mosaic.ts: only when a face or detail region exists and the cell is outside all regions, multiply lambda by bgCutFactor. When bgCutFactor > 1, disallow SUB outside regions. Without regions the output stays bit-identical.
Diagnostics: count splitCellsInRegions and subCellsInRegions exactly from data.kind. StepCompute shows 'Zellen mit Schnitt: X (davon Y in markierten Bereichen)'.

StepShapes: add a slider 'Schnitte außerhalb markierter Bereiche' from 'viele' (×1) to 'wenige' (×6), shown only when regions exist. Add a preset 'Schnitte auf Gesicht konzentrieren' (×3) and the hint to mark hair and contours as detail regions.

Accents: after assignment, collect stones whose analysed colour is more than ΔE 10 from their assigned colour. Group them greedily by ΔE76 < 6, keep groups of at least 2 stones, and put the top 3 in diagnostics.missingAccents {lab, hex, stones, meanDE, cellIds}. The suggested colour is the measured mean.

pinnedColors (the field from wave 3, passed by w4-progress-engine): in auto and auto-snap mode, run k-means with k − pinned and add the pinned colours unchanged (snapped to the nearest material in auto-snap). The existing unused-colour filter may drop them; StepColors then says the colour was not needed.

StepColors: add a pinned-colour list (add a hex, remove). StepCompute and StepColors show missingAccents, e.g. '8 Steine (z. B. Pupillen) ohne passende Farbe (ΔE 13,6) – Vorschlag #1D1F1B', with the stone IDs and an 'Als Pflichtfarbe übernehmen' button. That button only changes settings, so the project becomes stale.

Optional contourContinuity:
- Store each LINE cell's line in page coordinates.
- For the left and top neighbours, find anchor points on the joint midline and give a bonus of 0.6·λ·NS to candidates on the existing 0.5 mm grid that pass within 0.5 mm of an anchor. Halve the bonus inside faces.
- Do not add off-grid offsets.
acceptance: Portrait sample with its face region, bgCutFactor 3: cut cells outside the region drop by ≥30 % and cut cells inside drop by ≤25 %. Without regions the output equals golden for every factor.

Portrait at 32 colours: missingAccents contains an entry with L* < 15 and at least 2 stones. After pinning its hex, the pupil stones' ΔE00 is ≤ 3 and meanDeltaE rises by ≤ 0.05. A pinned hex appears unchanged in the palette whenever stones use it.

contourContinuity off equals golden. When on, on the portrait sample at 5×5 mm: the share of facing cut pairs that align within 1 mm is ≥ 65 %, distinct cut-template signatures rise by ≤ 10 %, and meanDeltaE rises by ≤ 0.1.
All count and geometry invariants hold, and the golden fixture is updated deliberately.
packages.risk: Effort L. Keep all three features off or neutral by default so existing projects compute the same unless the user opts in.

packages.title: Laying workbench: section focus, brush/rectangle marking, next stone, undo taps, material view switch
packages.goal: At the work table, the user can focus on one section and see live open counts per colour. They can mark stones by tap, brush or rectangle, undo mistakes, and step through 'next stone' cards that show the cut instructions. The material and shopping view gets its own full-width tab.
steps: Move MaterialCalc out of StepPlan into MaterialCalc.tsx without changing its behaviour. Add a top-level Segmented control 'Verlegen | Material & Einkauf' above the viewer layout. The material view renders full width without the viewer.

Section focus: in laying mode with a section selected, pass focusRange={sec} to the Viewer. A tap outside shows 'Stein gehört zu Abschnitt X – wechseln?'.
Colour chips from progressByColor for the section or the whole project, e.g. '06 · 37/112 offen'. Tapping a chip sets focusColor.
SectionLegend takes laid counts from progressByColor, not from the worker stats.

Marking modes Tippen | Malen | Rechteck:
- Malen: onPaint sets bits per piece.
- Rechteck: confirm 'N Steine als verlegt markieren?', then setRangePlaced.
- After each gesture call api.touchProgress(dirtyCells).
- Undo stack of 50 entries: piece toggles, plus progress slices for ranges. 'Rückgängig (n)' button.
- Status line, e.g. 'AP034 als verlegt markiert', plus the flash highlight.
- 'Abschnitt fertig' asks for confirmation when the section is partly laid.

Next-stone card, sticky at the bottom on phones:
- Content: ID, colour code and swatch, size, and the cut text from the exported cutInstruction. Export it from StoneDialog with no other change there. If a piece does not fit, show cut.notFit.
- Buttons: '✓ verlegt & weiter', 'zurück', 'überspringen', 'Reihe fertig' (row order only), 'Details' (opens StoneDialog).
- Order toggle Reihe/Farbe. Remember the section and order in localStorage inside try/catch.
- Screen wake lock, feature-detected and re-requested on visibilitychange.
Add a 'PDF {sec}' shortcut: set rec.pdfOptions.sectionIds = [sec.id] through api.update and navigate the hash to /pdf. Wrap the CSV export in await + catch with a visible error message.
acceptance: Unit tests: for the 4 samples, progressByColor totals per section sum to progressOf. layingOrder visits every piece of the range exactly once. Undo restores exact counts, including partly laid sections.

e2e: select B2, turn on laying mode, tap inside A1: placed-count is unchanged. Three times '✓ verlegt & weiter' then Rückgängig: placed-count is 2. A rectangle drag adds exactly that range's pieces. Finding 'ZZ9999' shows the not-found message. The Material tab has no horizontal page overflow at 1440 px.
packages.risk: Effort L. The undo stack lives only for the session; say so in the UI. Make sure the paint and rectangle modes never fire from normal scrolling on phones.

packages.title: Instant progress counts, no stats storms, progress carried over on recompute, progress in project lists
packages.goal: A laying tap costs microseconds instead of a full grid rescan. Background statistics never pile up. Recomputing with an unchanged layout keeps laid stones that are provably identical. Project lists show the percentage laid. Pinned colours reach the compute.
steps:
progressIndex.ts:
- buildProgressIndex(layout, data, sections) in one pass: secOfRow, secOfCol, placed[], total[], plus a copy of the masks. It uses cellPieceCount only.
- applyDirty(index, data, dirtyCells): popcount difference against the stored mask, then update it.
Rebuild the index on computed, sections or version change. touchProgress(dirtyCells) applies the deltas, or rebuilds when no cells are given. The progress memo reads the index.

Stats: remove progressVersion from the stats effect deps. Keep one stats job in flight; while it runs, a new request only sets a dirty flag, and one more job runs when the current one returns. When the inputs change, cancel an outdated running job with cancelChannel('stats') and ignore the 'abgebrochen' rejection.

db.ts: add meta.progressSummary {placed, total}. Write it with every progress save and clear it on recompute. Projects.tsx and the Home recent cards show 'NN % verlegt' with a mini ProgressBar only when the field exists.
compute params: pass pinnedColors from rec.settings.pinnedColors, converted to FixedColor (lab from hex).
acceptance: Vitest: after random toggles, setCellPlaced, setRangePlaced and kind/colour edits, the index equals progressOf per section and in total.
Carry-over: recomputing with identical settings keeps 100 % of laid stones. A joint change keeps 0 and reports it. A piece whose colour changed is reset and listed.

e2e: 12 laying taps 2 s apart on a project of about 1.4M stones post at most 2 stats worker messages (counted via an init script) and no tap long task over 50 ms on desktop. After marking a section, 'Meine Projekte' shows the percentage.
packages.risk: Effort M-L. Never carry over a laid bit unless it is proven identical (requirement 18). Old projects simply show no percentage until they are opened.

packages.title: PDF sheet structure: no paper-wasting strips, cut templates traceable from every sheet, code plans for tiny stones
packages.goal: Sheets are split evenly with no thin strips, and the page count is predictable through a shared planner. Every cut piece on a sheet points to its template T#. Sheets whose stones are too small for 1:1 codes get matching code-plan pages.
steps: pdfOptions.ts: move the sheet reserves (M 10, top 19, left 12, bottom 21) into exported SHEET_RESERVES and printableArea(opts). Add codePlan: 'auto' | 'always' | 'off' (default 'auto').

pdfPlan.ts:
- balancedSplit(pos, size, a, b, maxLen): greedy count, then cut lines spread evenly on grid lines.
- planSheets(layout, sections, opts) → exact cell ranges per sheet.
- planPdfPages(layout, sections, opts, piecesPerSection, templateGroups?) → {total, front, sectionCovers, sheets, cutLists, codePlans, templates, coords}. It uses the same constants and the rows-per-page rules of the generator.
generatePdf uses planSheets.
Sections that fit on one sheet get a compact 'Abschnittsübersicht' block instead of a full cover, packed several per page. Multi-sheet sections keep their cover.

T# on sheets:
- For each cut piece, look up the T# from tpl.bySig (signature from pieceCutInfo).
- Print it as a small second line when it fits (about 4.5 mm on paper).
- Otherwise draw a doc.circle callout with a plain number.
- After each sheet with cut or uncoded pieces, add a 'Zuschnittliste Blatt A1-n' page (pure sheetCutList, exported) with the columns: No, ID, code, shape, T# or 'T512 (nicht im PDF)', outer size.
- Template boxes list occurrences per sheet instead of 12 IDs.
- Apply the same '(nicht im PDF)' rule in the coordinate list.

Code plan:
- Export labelOk(piece, s), used by the sheet drawing code.
- When a 1:1 sheet has unlabelled stones and codePlan allows it, add code pages right after it. They cover exactly the same cell range at k = the smallest integer ≥ 2 such that every stone passes labelOk.
- Title: 'Codeplan zu Blatt A1-1 (Teil i/n) – NICHT maßstäblich (k:1)'.
- No crosses, no 'deckungsgleich' hint and no 'Kontrollstrecke', but a clear marker text.
- Draw thin guide lines every 10 cells on both the sheet and the code pages.
acceptance: planPdfPages(...).total equals doc.getNumberOfPages() for the 4 samples, on A4 and A3, with coordinates and templates on and off.
No sheet is narrower than 40 % of the printable width unless its section is.

Every cut piece in the selected sections appears exactly once on its sheet's cut list or carries an on-piece T#, and its T# equals bySig.get(signature).no. No referenced T# exceeds templateLimit without '(nicht im PDF)'.

With 2 mm tiles at 1:1 and codePlan auto, the code pages contain exactly one code per piece and the per-colour code counts equal stats. The fills on the 1:1 sheets still equal stats (existing test; code pages excluded by their marker).
packages.risk: Effort L. Section IDs and sheet numbering must stay stable for a given layout. Keep the 1:1 registration exactly as today.

packages.title: Offline face suggestions when the browser has no FaceDetector
packages.goal: For the user's own portraits, the app suggests a face region and an eye-band detail region offline, including in the APK. Suggestions are clearly marked and are applied only after the user confirms them.
steps: Vendor pico.js (MIT, about 6 KB) and the facefinder cascade (about 240 KB) with their licence. Do NOT add puploc unless its licence is confirmed.

faceDetect.ts: detectFacesGray(gray, w, h) → {x, y, w, h, score}[] normalised to 0..1, with cluster_detections and a quality threshold. face.worker.ts runs it on the 640 px editor image and loads the cascade via new URL('./facefinder.bin', import.meta.url).
vite.config.ts: add 'bin' to the workbox globPatterns so the cascade is precached for offline use.

RegionEditor:
- Use FaceDetector first when it exists, otherwise pico.
- Run once automatically when the shapes step opens with no regions; the button stays too.
- Suggestions live in local state, drawn dashed, with 'automatisch erkannt – bitte prüfen (Sicherheit x %)' and Übernehmen/Verwerfen.
- Accepting adds the expanded face ellipse and an eye-band detail region labelled 'geschätzt'.
- Selected regions get move and resize handles with 44 px hit areas.
- With no detection, say 'Kein Gesicht gefunden'.
- Text states that only frontal human faces are detected.
acceptance: Unit test: a small public-domain real portrait fixture gives one detection whose centre lies inside a hand-labelled face box. landscape.png and city.png give no detection above the threshold. The synthetic portrait does not crash.
Playwright: after the service worker installs, an offline context still produces suggestions on the shapes step. Nothing is added to the regions until Übernehmen is clicked.
packages.risk: Effort M. Detection quality is unverified; if the fixture test fails, ship the manual flow only and document that. Never auto-apply a region.

waves.name: Wave 5 – Undo/redo & stone editing, scale performance, PDF content, shopping view, target colours, PDF export UI

packages.title: Undo/redo for every edit, non-modal stone inspector, lighter/darker, persistent comparison reference
packages.goal: Every stone, shape, freeform and palette edit can be undone and redone safely. Stone details open beside the mosaic on large screens and as a phone-friendly sheet on small ones. 'Make this stone a lighter blue' takes one click. The photo comparison survives a reload.
steps: edits.ts: add snapshotCell(data, idx), which deep-copies kind, c1, c2, sub, line, free and progress. Add restoreCell and cellEquals.

useProject:
- api.editCell(idx, mutate) snapshots before and after, pushes only real changes and clears redo.
- api.paletteOp(kind, fn) for add, update, remove and replace.
- undo() and redo() apply an entry only if the current cell equals entry.after; otherwise drop it and show a toast.
- Clear both stacks on compute.
- Keyboard shortcuts: Ctrl/Cmd+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z and Ctrl+Y, ignored while an input has focus.
- Persist a ≤2048 px JPEG of the processed reference at compute time (an ImageRecord field in db.ts) and decode it on load. Offer 'Referenz neu erzeugen' for older projects, using adjust from computedWith.

StoneDialog:
- Route every edit through api.editCell.
- 'Heller' and 'Dunkler' pick an existing palette colour with |ΔL*| ≥ 3, Δa*b* ≤ 10 and ΔH ≤ 8, nearest step first. If none exists, the button is disabled with the hint to add one in step 5.
- Keep the similarity order anchored to the colour the stone had when the inspector opened.
- Show name and ΔE under the selected swatch, and ▲/▼ markers for lighter and darker.
- Laid toggle as a large button with aria-pressed.

Layout:
- At ≥980 px, StoneDialog renders as variant 'panel' in place of the legend aside of StepPreview and StepPlan: sticky, scrolls on its own, no backdrop, canvas stays interactive.
- Below 980 px it stays a modal. At ≤600 px the order is: summary with the laid toggle, then colour row (12 nearest plus 'Alle Farben'), then cut template, then shape, then position and neighbours.
StepPreview and StepPlan: Rückgängig/Wiederholen buttons with counters. StepPreview uses FindStone.tsx and api.reference for the comparison slider.
acceptance: Vitest: a SUB cell [3,5,7,9] with progress 101 changed to FULL, then undone, restores exactly, and stats equal the pre-edit stats. Removing the portrait's most-used colour and undoing restores packMosaic bytes exactly. The journal respects its byte cap.
e2e: change a stone 03→02, Ctrl+Z restores 03, Ctrl+Shift+Z gives 02 again.
e2e: 'Heller' on a pale-blue stone picks a same-hue lighter code, or is disabled with the hint.
e2e: after compute and reload, the comparison slider still shows the photo.
packages.risk: Effort L. The journal must never restore stale state over newer changes, hence the after-equals check. It is session-only; README wording follows in wave 7.

packages.title: Single-pass statistics, 8-13x faster with identical results
packages.goal: Totals, per-section figures, per-colour and per-material figures, and the new quality counters come from one pass over the grid. Results are exactly the same as before, and large projects show counts seconds sooner.
steps: Add computeAllStats(layout, data, palette, materials, opts, grid) → {total, perSection}. It uses precomputed colClass and rowClass (toFixed(4) equivalence, as today), rawClass per colour, and rowSec/colSec lookups.
Integer cache keys for FULL, DIAG and SUB. LINE keeps an exact key from the Float32 bit pattern of nx, ny and d, never quantised. FREE is never cached.

Accumulate the total in the same pass, not as a sum of sections, so floats and perSize tie order are identical. Move the post-loop code into finalizeStats(), used for each section and the total. Keep computeStats as a thin wrapper.
New counters: thinPieces (minCaliperWidth < shapes.minPieceMm, for automatic pieces; freeform counted separately), overlapCells (summed piece area > cell area), invalidPieces (analyzeCut invalid).
compute.worker.ts stats message: replace the per-section computeStats calls with one computeAllStats call. Update protocol.ts types.
acceptance: Equivalence test: JSON.stringify(computeAllStats) equals the old computeStats for the total and every section. Inputs: random mosaics with DIAG, generator-style and manually edited LINE (any angle or offset), SUB 2/3, FREE, cut-end edges, materials with different raw sizes, and progress bits.
Scratch bench: 2M cells take ≤ 1/6 of the old total-plus-sections time. Record the number in the PR.
typecheck and test are green.
packages.risk: Effort M. Keep the reference implementation in the test so later changes cannot drift.

packages.title: Smooth panning and zooming via a cached back buffer
packages.goal: Panning and zooming stay smooth on tablets and phones at every zoom level, with pixels identical to a fresh render, and edits and taps appear immediately.
steps: render.ts: add an option to skip the sections and highlight passes. Move them into drawOverlay(ctx, …).

Viewer: keep an off-screen base canvas about 1.5-2x the viewport in device pixels, rendered with the unchanged renderMosaic. Its cache key covers every field in the draw-effect dependencies plus dpr, scale and the background colour.

Pan: snap ox/oy to multiples of 1/dpr and blit the base at an integer device-pixel offset each frame, then draw the overlays. Re-render the base, or the newly exposed strips through clip plus a restricted View, when the margin runs out.
Zoom: draw the scaled base during the gesture and render exactly 120-150 ms after the last zoom event; a scaled frame must never be the final image.

Invalidation: a key change re-renders the whole base. For single-stone edits and progress taps (version or progressVersion with dirty cells, otherwise full), re-render only the cell rectangle ±joint/2 through clip. A full re-render is always an allowed fallback.
acceptance: Pixel test: a base blitted at an integer offset equals a fresh renderMosaic of the shifted view (max channel difference ≤ 1).
e2e: after a colour edit and after a laying tap, the canvas pixel at that stone changes at once.
pan benchmark (TABLET=1, THROTTLE=4, steps 4-18): median rAF callback < 8 ms (today 80-101 ms).
packages.risk: Effort M. A stale cache could show a wrong colour; keep invalidation conservative and tested. Drawing stays in render.ts so the PDF and preview match.

packages.title: Per-sheet legends, readable cut templates, complete compact coordinates, readable overview
packages.goal: Each laying sheet carries its own colour key and stone counts. Cut-template dimensions never overlap text. The coordinate appendix covers 100 % of stones in a fraction of the pages. The overview of large projects stays readable.
steps:
Per-sheet legend:
- Data from computeStats(range = the sheet, the shared cache).
- Header 'Steine auf diesem Blatt: N, davon K zugeschnitten', then chips of about 45×4.5 mm with swatch, code, material colour number or short name, and ×count.
- Place it in the free band below the joint label, otherwise in a free right column, otherwise on a 'Legende zu Blatt X' page that follows. Never truncate.
- Draw swatches as 'F' plus a separate 'S', never 'FD'. No 'Kontrollstrecke' on continuation pages.

templateLayout.ts: pure layoutTemplate(ci, group, boxW, measure).
- Measure the text first; warnings come first in the text block.
- Choose zoom from [10, 8, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1.5, 1].
- Dimension lines at a fixed 2.5 mm paper offset, with extension lines, labels parallel to the edge and an outward normal from the orientation.
- Collision pass against title, text, the 1:1 contour, other labels and cut lines; leader lines as fallback.
- Wrapped lines advance by lines × 2.4 mm. No dropped lines; the row height follows the content.
drawTemplate only renders the result.

coords.ts: buildCompactCoords(layout, data, palette, sections, opts).
- Column table and row table, with 'Zuschnitt' marks on edge columns and rows.
- Per section, one colour-run line per row, e.g. 'K: 001–006 → 09 · 007 ◆ …'.
- Exception rows for non-FULL pieces, FULL pieces that need a cut, and pieces whose raw size differs from the grid tile.
- A control sum equal to section stats pieces; on mismatch draw an error box.
pdfOptions: coordMode 'compact' | 'perStone' | 'off', default 'compact'. includeCoords=false maps to 'off'. coordLimit applies only to perStone. Update planPdfPages.

Overview map-grid mode: when the median section is under 10 mm on paper, or labels would exceed 70 % of a section, draw thin section lines plus column numbers and row letters along the edges, with a caption, and no per-cell boxes. Otherwise use font-relative label boxes in the corner. Selected sections get a thicker outline and a light fill. Each section cover gets a small locator thumbnail (one embedded image alias).
acceptance: The per-sheet legend counts, summed over a section's sheets, equal secStats.perColor pieces. The existing per-colour fill test stays green and unchanged.

layoutTemplate on 3/5/10/12 mm configurations and one 20 mm-raw material configuration: no label box intersects the title, the text block, the 1:1 contour or another label; each label equals f1(ci.edges[i]); text never exceeds the box.

Compact coordinates: every stone's (X, Y, colour) can be reconstructed from the tables plus the exceptions and equals cellPieces. The 200×100 cm, 5 mm case needs ≤ 70 coordinate pages (today 329 pages covering only 35 %).
A 10000×5000 mm project with 300 mm sections uses map-grid mode.
packages.risk: Effort L. The compact coordinate format changes the documented output; keep perStone available. planPdfPages must stay equal to the actual page count.

packages.title: Full-width material and shopping view with exact per-material buying list
packages.goal: The Material & Einkauf tab shows what to buy per material: packs, stock and shortfall, cost, and missing materials. It exports a shopping CSV and prints cleanly.
steps:
Stat row:
- Steine gesamt.
- Rohsteine inkl. Reserve, labelled as a safe upper bound.
- Kosten, with two decimals and the 'unvollständig' badge.
- Fugenmasse, labelled Schätzung.
- The reserve chips.

packages.title: Store each stone's photo target colour for exact deviation maps
packages.goal: Each stone's measured photo colour is persisted with the mosaic, so deviation can be computed live and stays correct after manual edits.
steps:
types.ts MosaicData: add optional tLab1 (Uint8Array, 3 per cell), tLab2 (for DIAG/LINE cells) and tSubLab Map<idx, Uint8Array>, reusing the existing quantisation (qL/qAB).

waves.name: Wave 6 – Deviation map & batch editing, real fine tiles, colour measuring, streaming CSV, final PDF wiring

packages.title: Deviation map, largest-deviation list, batch recolouring and PNG preview export
packages.goal: The user can see where the mosaic deviates most from the photo, jump to those stones, correct whole areas in one undoable step, and save the preview as an image.

BatchPanel: Viewer mode 'rect' selects a cell range; the scope can also be the current section or the whole project. Actions, each one journal entry through api.editCell/paletteOp:
- 'Farbe A → B' via replaceColor, with a dry-run count first.

packages.title: Fine stones in real buyable sizes for faces and details (mixed sizes, stage 1)
packages.goal: Subdivided cells can use real small tiles of a buyable size, counted as uncut stones of their own material. Fine regions force finer stones where the user wants them, so requirement 3 and requirement 5 are served by actual planning, not just by cutting large stones.
steps:
types.ts: add Region.type 'fine', PaletteColor.fineMaterialId?, and ShapeOptions.fineTileMm?.
StepShapes: a 'Feinstein-Größe' select that offers the k ∈ {2,3} giving an exact size, fine = (w+g)/k − g. Other k values are shown honestly as 'wird aus dem Grundstein geschnitten'. The RegionEditor tool gets the 'fine' type (StepShapes passes the type option).

mosaic.ts: if the cell centre lies in a fine region and every subRect passes pieceCuttable, force SUB with the group means. Otherwise keep the normal choice and set Rec.FINER. Inside face and detail regions with subdivision on, lower the SUB penalty to at most the LINE cost (1.4·λ).

stats.ts: makeRawSizeFn(color, pieceW, pieceH) returns the fine material when the piece bbox matches its size within DIM_TOL; analyzeCut then reports exactRaw, i.e. uncut with yield 1. perColor and perMaterial get one row per (colour, raw size). Sub pieces with no matching fine material stay 'cut from base tile'.
StepColors: per colour, a second 'Feinstein-Material' select limited to materials of the fine size, with an auto-match by ΔE.
acceptance: Total pieces are unchanged when a fine material is assigned.
Sub pieces are uncut exactly when the fine material size equals the sub size. FULL stones of the same colour still use the base material, so notFitting stays 0.
On the portrait sample with a fine region over the eyes, at least 50 % of the cells in that region are SUB, and all invariants hold.
The golden fixture is unchanged for projects without fine regions.
packages.risk: Effort M-L. Zones with their own grid (stage 2) are deferred. The tiles-step honesty badge stays until then.

packages.title: Measure material colours from a photo on any device
packages.goal: APK and tablet users can measure a tile's colour from a camera photo, with glare rejection and an optional white or grey reference. The result is stored and shown as a measured approximation.
steps:
colorMeasure.ts (pure):
- samplePatch(img, cx, cy, r): drop clipped pixels (any channel ≥ 250), trim the top and bottom 10 % by L*, average in linear sRGB. Returns lab, hex, n, clippedFrac and spreadDE.
- whiteBalanceGains(refLin, 'paper' | 'grey18'): 'paper' corrects only the colour cast and keeps luminance; 'grey18' targets 0.18.
- applyGains.

MeasureColorDialog:
- File input with capture=environment.
- Decode with createImageBitmap(file, {imageOrientation:'from-image'}) at about 2000 px; zoomable.
- Optional reference tap. A clipped reference is rejected with 'Referenz überbelichtet'.
- Tile tap with an adjustable patch.
- Shows the photo crop next to the swatch, HEX and Lab, ΔE to the current value, and the spread, with a warning when the spread is above about 4.
- Saving requires 'Übernehmen'.

Materials form: the button is always visible and the eyedropper is an extra where it exists. Store Material.colorSource (contract from wave 5). Typing a HEX by hand sets 'manual'. The material list shows a tag 'gemessen (Näherung, Referenz: Papier, ±x ΔE)'. Append the CSV fields to materialsCsv; old CSV files still import.
acceptance: Unit tests: a synthetic flat patch with 10 % white glints and dark border pixels comes back within ΔE < 1. A colour cast on the reference is removed by the gains. A clipped reference is rejected.

packages.title: Streaming CSV for millions of stones and paper-matched section presets
packages.goal: 'Alle Koordinaten als CSV' works at 5M stones without freezing or failing silently, and includes template numbers and correct colour names. Section sizes can match the paper with one click.
steps: csv.ts: add buildCsvChunks(...) as a Generator<string> yielding a header and then bands of about 20k rows. Keep buildCsv as a join of the chunks. Columns use paletteDisplayName and write the Zuschnitt value as 'ja (T12)' using the collectTemplates numbering. Section exports iterate the section's own range instead of filtering the whole grid. Throw a translated error if maxColorIndex ≥ palette.length.

StepPlan exportCsv: show progress and an Abbrechen button. Prepend the BOM. Pass the result to downloadBlob and show SaveResultNote. When there are more than 1,048,576 rows, warn that Excel and LibreOffice cannot open that many.

StepPlan section settings: add presets '1 Blatt' and '2×2 Blätter', set from printableArea(rec.pdfOptions)/sheetScale. Add a hint when the current sections leave thin strips (using planSheets). Ask for confirmation if laying progress exists, because section IDs change.

packages.title: Exact page counts, labelled parts, coordinate mode choice, PDF on the fast stats engine

A part PDF of a 6-section project shows 'Teil 2/3' in its headers. Its template T numbers equal those of a full export, and summed over all parts the stone fills per colour equal stats.

waves.name: Wave 7 – Documentation, honest limitations & end-to-end consolidation

packages.title: README limitations, feature docs and one e2e entry point
packages.goal: The README describes exactly what MosaicPlan now does and does not do (requirement 18), and one command runs every end-to-end check.
steps: Document the raw-tile count semantics (a safe upper bound per identical cut shape), the dither trade-off, the cut minimum-width rule, the export/import with materials, and the PDF part and code-plan features.
e2e/run-e2e.cjs: keep the existing flow, then run every e2e/*.e2e.cjs in sequence with a summary. Exit non-zero on any failure.
tests/w7-i18n-ext.test.ts: assert that no two ext files override the same key, and that every ext file has key and placeholder parity across de, en and tr.
Run the full suite: typecheck, test, build, e2e, and `npm run android:sync`. Fix any small leftover integration seams. Record the results in the PR.

README lists every limitation that remains and states which checks were device-unverified.
The duplicate-override test passes.
packages.risk: Effort S-M. This package is last because it reflects the merged state; it must not change behaviour.

deferred: Grout compensation in computeMosaic (algo-quality#0, part 4). Both reviewers called it optional and off by default, and recommending a grout plus an honest preview gives most of the benefit. Changing the factory grout default from #BDB8AE to #808080 is deferred too; the recommendation never overwrites the user's choice.

Linear-light averaging of stone target colours (algo-quality#10). Measured gains are within k-means noise on natural photos. Revisit it together with linear-light resizing in imageOps, with a measured A/B benchmark.

Mixed tile sizes stage 2: zones with their own grid (spec-gaps#2). Wave 6 delivers stage 1, real fine-tile materials for k×k sub-stones plus fine regions. Zones touch every per-cell structure (progress mask, IDs, sections, hit-testing, PDF), and the tiles-step badge stays honest until then.

Movable section boundaries and a seam optimiser (spec-gaps#9). This is impact 2-3 and needs new settings across layout, viewer, worker and PDF. Paper-matched section presets (wave 6) cover the main paper-waste pain.
Full SVG export of plans and templates (spec-gaps#12). The vector PDF at 1:1 or custom paper already covers plotters. Only PNG preview export is built (wave 6).

Diff-based incremental statistics in a worker that keeps its own mosaic copy, and dirty-pixel overview updates (performance-scale#5, parts 2-3). They are replaced by the 8-13x single-pass stats (wave 5), coalesced stats jobs and O(1) progress counters (wave 4). Revisit only if 5M-stone edits are still slower than about 1 s.
Splitting the shape analysis across several workers (performance-scale#7, part b). The hot-loop fix gives about 4x. SharedArrayBuffer is not available without COOP/COEP headers.
One CSV per section, delivered as a ZIP (performance-scale#1). Streaming CSV plus the Excel row-limit warning are built; a store-only ZIP can follow if users ask.
Automatic stock-constrained recolouring (spec-gaps#4, part 4). It would change how the image looks and is often impossible. Exact shortfall and shopping lists are built instead.

Error-driven k-means swap refinement and detail-weighted palette samples (algo-quality#6, optional part). Measured gains were inconsistent. Pinned accent colours confirmed by the user are built instead.
Dither error diffusion through split/SUB cells, serpentine scanning and face/edge damping (algo-quality#1). Measured as useless or harmful.
Global cut budget, 'max. Schnittzellen' (algo-quality#3, phase 2). The background cut factor in wave 4 gives most of the value.
Image-level Canny/polyline contour extraction (algo-quality#5). Unproven, and it would defeat template reuse. Only the opt-in grid-preserving continuity bonus is built.
Haptic feedback with the VIBRATE permission (ux-mobile-android#2). The text status line and flash highlight already give feedback.
A native 'pause' flush registry through @capacitor/app (ux-mobile-android#1). beforeunload with commit(), visibilitychange and minimizeApp already cover saving.
MediaPipe face detection. Its 14.6 MB wasm exceeds the PWA precache limit; pico.js is used instead (wave 4).
Colour-chart sheet mode for measuring many tiles from one photo (spec-gaps#7, phase 2).
First-fit-decreasing packing of mixed-width strips into shared raw tiles (correctness-core#5, optional). The current per-shape-group count is a safe upper bound.
Mixed page orientations per section and tighter print margins (pdf-print#4). Mixed orientations risk print-dialog auto-scaling, which breaks 1:1. Smaller margins clip on common printers.
Undo history that persists across reloads (ux-desktop#7). The journal is in memory for the session only, and the README will say so.

kept.title: Grout colour dominates how the finished mosaic looks, but colour matching ignores it (the default light grout washes out every photo)
kept.problem: computeMosaic matches each stone to the photo as if stones covered 100 % of the surface. With 5 mm stones and a 1 mm joint the grout covers 30.6 % of the area (8 mm/1 mm: 21 %). From a normal viewing distance the eye mixes stones and grout in linear light, so the default grout #BDB8AE (src/core/types.ts:212) lifts every dark area (suit, hair, pupils) and desaturates skin. The diagnostics shown on the compute step (StepCompute.tsx:90-94, fed by track() in mosaic.ts) compare only the stone colour with the cell mean. They report 'ΔE ≈ 1.6–3.5', which hides the problem.
kept.evidence: Script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/algo-quality/exp-grout.ts, output in .../algo-quality/out/results/exp-grout.txt. Perceived ΔE00 = Gaussian blur over the full render including grout, σ = 2 pitches, linear light, compared with the blurred photo. Default grout #BDB8AE: obama 40 cm/5 mm 12.8 mean / 29.4 p95; astronaut 10.8/30.0; coffee 12.7/24.8; synthetic portrait sample 11.5/23.9. Same stones with grout #404040: 6.0/8.5, 6.7/9.1, 6.1/7.9, 5.7/8.1. Prototype .../algo-quality/exp-grout-comp.ts (output .../out/results/exp-grout-comp.txt): stone target t' = (t − (1−f)·g)/f in linear RGB, then k-means and matching. Dark grout plus full compensation reaches 2.0/5.1 (obama), 2.7/7.2 (astronaut), 2.3/5.6 (coffee). With the light default grout, compensation cannot help (11.5/28.8) because the darks are out of reach. Visual: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/algo-quality/out/grout-distance-view.png (source | app default | dark grout | dark grout + compensation, downscaled to simulate distance). Photos: public-domain NASA/US-gov portraits and CC0 skimage samples in .../algo-quality/dl/photos/.
kept.proposal: (1) S – Recommend a grout colour. Evaluate a short list of real grout colours (white, light grey, beige, mid grey, anthracite, black) on the downsampled working image in linear light, with stone coverage f = tileW·tileH/((tileW+g)(tileH+g)) from the layout. Preselect the colour with the lowest perceived ΔE and show that number in the joint step (StepGeometry). (2) M – Optional grout-aware colour targets in computeMosaic. Before k-means and matching, convert each cell/piece target to linear RGB and apply t' = clamp((t − (1−f_s)·g)/f_s), where f_s = 1 − s·(1−f) and s is a 'Fernwirkung' strength slider (0–100 %, default 50 %). Match by ΔE00(t', palette). The stone dialog keeps showing the original photo colour, so nothing is hidden. (3) S – Add an honest 'Fernwirkung ΔE' diagnostic (blur including grout) next to the existing ΔE. Expected: perceived mean ΔE about −50 % from the grout choice alone and about −80 % with compensation on real photos.
corrected:

- Show the best candidate with its ΔE next to the grout colour picker, plus a one-click 'Übernehmen' button.

2) (S) Honest distance preview.
- In buildOverviewRGBA (src/core/render.ts:93), blend each cell's colour with the grout colour in linear light, using that cell's coverage f_cell. Then the zoomed-out view (render.ts:165) shows the real effect instead of stone colours only.

3) (S) Distance diagnostic in StepCompute. Add a second row, 'Farbabweichung aus Entfernung inkl. Fuge (Schätzung)': mean and p95 ΔE00 of f_cell·stone + (1−f_cell)·grout against the photo cell, computed in linear light. f_cell = (sum of the cell's piece polygon areas from cellPieces/subRects) / ((colW+joint)·(rowH+joint)). kept.title: Dithering scatters off-colour stones (orange in cheeks, black in hair); restricting it to similar colours keeps most of the benefit
kept.problem: On real photos, reducing to the palette is the largest error source. With unlimited colours the same geometry reaches a perceived ΔE of 0.29–0.32; with 32 k-means colours it is 1.38–1.93 (4–6×). This shows up as large flat patches and false contours in smooth backgrounds and skin. The only remedy, Floyd-Steinberg (mosaic.ts:493-519), picks the colour nearest to target + error from the whole palette, with errors clamped only at ±25. It therefore drops stones of a different hue into faces and hair. It also diffuses error only through FULL cells (split and SUB cells neither receive nor pass it on) and scans in one direction only. The default is 0 %, so most users get the banding.

kept.title: Edge cuts point the right way but do not join up between neighbouring stones, so contours look staggered
kept.problem: Each cell chooses its LINE cut independently (mosaic.ts:283-349): orientation from the cell's own gradient tensor, 3 angles in 15° steps, and offsets on a 0.5 mm grid. The orientation is accurate, so the 15° steps are adequate. But neighbouring cells' offsets do not line up, so a contour is drawn as short segments that stop at a joint and continue shifted in the next stone. A mosaicist would cut the contour as one continuous line.

Script .../algo-quality/exp-cuts.ts (.../out/results/exp-cuts.txt): only 22–42 % of cut-line ends on an inner cell edge continue (within 1 mm) in the neighbouring cell (coffee 22.4 %, obama 30.8 %, astronaut 36.6 %, portrait sample 41 %). Prototype 'neighbour bonus 0.6' in .../algo-quality/exp-proto.ts: score −0.6·λ·NS for each endpoint that matches an already decided left/top neighbour. Continuity rises for obama 30.8→45.9 %, astronaut 36.6→48.4 %, portrait 41→47.7 %, while perceived ΔE changes by +0.07, −0.01 and −0.11.
kept.proposal: Short term (S/M): in the LINE search, also try lines that pass exactly through the left/top neighbour's endpoint, in addition to the 0.5 mm grid, and add a continuity bonus. Cells are already processed in row-major order inside each 64-cell tile, so left/top neighbours are always decided. Longer term: extract edge polylines once at image level (Canny on L* with hysteresis, linking, Douglas–Peucker at about 0.5 tile). Then derive each crossed cell's cut from the polyline segment inside it, which gives continuous contours by construction. Pieces stay exact half-plane-clipped polygons, so cut templates remain correct. Track the continuity metric above in a test; target > 70 %.

2. **Find anchor points.** Before the offset loop, check the left neighbour (idx−1) and the top neighbour (idx−cols). If one is LINE, extend its line to the joint midline (x = r.x − g/2 for left, y = r.y − g/2 for top). If that point lies inside this cell's side, keep it as an anchor.

4. **Do not add exact-through-endpoint offsets.** Measured, they bring no extra continuity but 18–41 % more distinct cut templates (`pdf.ts:62` groups templates by signature). Leave every other check as it is (`pieceCuttable`, `lineSplit`), so cut templates stay exact.

**Test.** Add a vitest case on the portrait sample (400 mm, 5×5 mm tiles, 1 mm joint, face region):
- Count pairs where both neighbours have a cut facing the shared edge. Compare the two lines at the joint midline.
- Assert at least 65 % line up within 1 mm. Today it is about 60 %; with the bonus about 69 %.
- Assert `diagnostics.meanDeltaE` does not rise by more than 0.1.
- Assert the number of distinct cut-template signatures rises by no more than 10 %.

Do not use "% of all cut ends" as the measure. About 40 % of ends border uncut stones, and that is not misalignment.

**Optional later (L effort, unproven).** Trace edge polylines across the whole image and derive each cell's cut from them, still with offsets snapped to the 0.5 mm grid.

Low priority (impact 2, effort S/M). Keep the 0.5 mm offset grid and the 15° angles (README.md:151) so cut templates still repeat.

1) Add a "Konturen durchgehend schneiden" option (a ShapeOptions flag, default OFF) to the shapes step (StepShapes.tsx).

2) In the LINE search in mosaic.ts:300-347, for the left neighbour (idx−1) and the top neighbour (idx−cols), when that neighbour is a LINE cell with the same angle:
- Compute the collinear offset: d* = d_nb + n·(c_nb − c), where c is the cell centre. Snap d* to the 0.5 mm grid.
- Add it to the candidate list only if it is not already there and it passes pieceCuttable.

3) Add a continuity bonus only for collinear matches. A match means the neighbour's line, extended across the joint along its own direction, meets this cell's endpoint within 0.6 mm, with an angle difference under 16°. Use weight 0.3-0.6·λ·NS. Do not apply the bonus inside face regions (inFace), or scale it down there, to protect requirement 6.

4) Do NOT add off-grid "through-endpoint" offsets. Measured: +16 to +56 template groups for under 1 percentage point of continuity gain (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/value-algo-quality-5/out/exp.txt).

kept.proposal: Weight palette samples by importance: w = area · (1 + 2·det) · faceWeight. Keep the swap only if total weighted ΔE00 (not squared) decreases. Seed near-black and near-white automatically when at least 0.2 % of samples have L* < 15 or > 95. Add a regression test: portrait-sample pupil ΔE < 6 while the global mean rises by no more than 0.05.

Add a post-Lloyd palette refinement in src/core/kmeans.ts, e.g. refinePalette(pts, w, centers, opts), and call it from mosaic.ts after kmeansLab for paletteMode 'auto' and 'auto-snap'.

1. Assign every sample with ΔE00, the same metric NearestColorMatcher uses. For each sample keep the best distance d1, the second-best d2 and the assigned centre a1.

2. Build candidate groups, in this order:

   - (b) Light extremes: samples with L* > 92 and d1 > 6.
   - (c) General outliers: cluster the samples with d1 > 10 into up to 4 groups with a small k-means.
   Each group needs at least 3 stones, counted by number, not by weight. The candidate colour is the group's weighted mean.

3. For each candidate:
   - Compute each palette colour's marginal loss as Σ w·(d2 − d1) over its members, and replace the colour with the smallest loss.
   - Accept the swap if the weighted mean ΔE00 (L1, not squared) rises by at most 0.05 for an extreme group (a or b), or does not rise at all for a general group (c).
   - Do NOT stop at the first rejected candidate. Allow at most about 4 accepted swaps.
   - Freeze accepted centres so further Lloyd steps cannot pull them back into the hair-brown cluster.

kept.title: "Neu berechnen" silently wipes laying progress and manual stone edits (no confirm, no undo)
kept.problem: Any trivial change after computing (e.g. brightness +1 in step 1) turns the project stale. The orange stale badge in the header jumps straight to step 7, and one click on "Neu berechnen" replaces the mosaic. That throws away all marked progress and every manual colour/shape/freeform edit, with no confirmation and no undo (the README says undo does not exist). The only warning is a grey, small-print line under the button.
kept.evidence:
Reproduction /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/ux-desktop/journey4.cjs, output in journey4.out: 'progress after marking A1 done: 51,4 %' -> 'stale badge visible after brightness +1: true' -> 'confirm dialogs shown on recompute: 0' -> 'progress after recompute: 0 %'. Screenshots shots/j4-03-stale.png, j4-04-recompute-screen.png, j4-05-progress-lost.png. Code: src/ui/project/useProject.ts compute() (~l.275-350) builds a fresh MosaicData and saveProgress() overwrites the stored progress. src/ui/project/StepCompute.tsx:78 shows compute.overwriteWarn only as

. src/ui/project/Workspace.tsx:55 makes the stale badge a direct button to the compute step.
kept.proposal: 1) In StepCompute's compute-btn onClick, when api.progress.total.placed > 0 or the project has manual edits, open a <Modal> (not window.confirm). Track manual edits with a new rec.meta.editCount, incremented in touchMosaic. The modal says: "X verlegte Steine und Y manuell geänderte Steine gehen verloren" and offers [Abbrechen] [Als Kopie neu berechnen] [Trotzdem neu berechnen]. The copy option calls duplicateProject() from src/storage/projects.ts, navigates to the copy and computes there. 2) Keep progress where it is provably still valid. If layoutParamsOf(old) equals layoutParamsOf(new), copy progress bits only for cells whose kind and piece count did not change (core/edits helper). Show how many were kept and how many reset; never guess for changed cells. 3) Make the stale badge open step 7 with an explanation of what changed, not a one-click path to data loss.

   - Edit counter: increment rec.meta.editCount in touchMosaic (useProject.ts:164). Reset it to 0 in compute() when building `next` (around l.331).
   - Modal text: "{placed} als verlegt markierte Steine und {edits} manuelle Änderungen gehen verloren."
   - Buttons: [Abbrechen] [Sicherungskopie anlegen und neu berechnen] [Trotzdem neu berechnen].

   - Make the overwrite warning at StepCompute.tsx:78 use the `warn` class and include the live placed count when progress > 0.

2) Restore the previous calculation (M). In compute(), before saveMosaic/saveProgress at l.346, write the old packed mosaic, the old progress and {palette, computedWith, diagnostics} to IndexedDB under `${id}#prev`. Offer a "Vorherige Berechnung wiederherstellen" button on step 7/8 while that key exists. Extend deleteProject (db.ts:104) and duplicateProject/exportProject to handle or skip the #prev keys, so nothing is left orphaned.

3) Do NOT copy progress bits by matching cell kind or piece count. A laid stone whose recomputed colour differs would be shown as laid in a colour that was never placed, which breaks requirement 18. If keeping progress is wanted later, do it as "pin laid cells" (effort L):
   - When layoutParamsOf(old) deep-equals layoutParamsOf(new), copy the complete old cell content (kind, c1/c2, sub, line, free, progress) for every cell with any progress bit set, overriding the new result.
   - Map the old colours into the new palette by exact HEX. Append any old colour that is missing as a new palette entry; never snap it to the nearest new colour.

   - Text (de/en/tr): "{placed} von {total} Steinen sind als verlegt markiert{edited>0 ? ` und ${edited} Positionen wurden manuell geändert` : ''}. Neu berechnen ersetzt den Plan."

   - Otherwise, for each cell and each piece, copy the laid bit only if all of these match: the kind; the SUB k and LINE [nx,ny,d] (exactly equal, or within 1e-4 mm); and the hex plus materialId of oldPalette[oldColor] and newPalette[newColor]. Compare palette entries, not indices.
   - For laid pieces that fail the check, set the bit to 0 and list them as "verlegt, aber im neuen Plan anders". Show cell ID, old colour code and new colour code, so the user can decide physically.
