5) Stale badge (S).
   - Parse rec.computedWith and diff it against computeKey(rec) by group: l = Größe/Steine/Fuge, a = Fotobearbeitung, sh = Formen, pm/cc/cp/mi = Farben, rg = Bereiche.
   - Show "Geändert seit letzter Berechnung: Fotobearbeitung (Helligkeit)" in step 7.
   - Add a [Änderungen verwerfen] action that restores the settings and adjust values stored in computedWith. That makes the stale state go away without recomputing, which works as an undo for accidental slider nudges.

kept.title: Steps 2-6 are blind: no picture of the mosaic until step 7, although computing takes only 0.25-1.4 s
kept.problem: Size, tile size, joint, colours and shapes are all chosen against numbers only ("Raster 34 × 42", "Fugenanteil 20,7 %"). The hobbyist cannot see how a 4 mm vs 8 mm tile or 16 vs 48 colours changes the picture without going to step 7, computing, looking at step 8 and coming back. Computing is fast enough for live feedback, so the separate compute step is mostly friction.
kept.evidence: Timing via the real UI, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/ux-desktop/journey5.out: 4,453 positions 251 ms; 12,322 positions 336 ms; 33,901 positions 832 ms; 194,886 positions 1,355 ms (compute plus navigation). The default 30×40 cm project shows 'Rechenzeit 0,1 s' (shots/j1-08-compute-result.png). Steps without any visual: shots/j1-05-size.png, j1-05-tiles.png, j1-05-joint.png, j1-05-colors.png. The right column holds only LayoutSummary (src/ui/project/StepGeometry.tsx:9-61).
kept.proposal: Keep the required 10 steps but make steps 2-6 live. Add useProject.previewCompute(): it runs the existing 'compute' worker job without persisting and without touching computedWith or progress, debounced about 600 ms on computeKey(rec) changes, and only when cols*rows < about 250k (above that, show a 'Vorschau aktualisieren' button). Render the result with renderFull() into a <LivePreview> canvas that becomes the main right-hand visual in StepSize/StepTiles/StepJoint/StepColors/StepShapes. LayoutSummary shrinks to a compact stat strip under it. Add an optional before/after toggle (photo vs mosaic). Step 7 then becomes 'Übernehmen/Berechnen' (commit), and the first commit can happen automatically when the user reaches step 8.
corrected:
Keep the 10 steps and add a live preview that is never saved, in steps 2-6.

1. Split useProject.compute() (src/ui/project/useProject.ts) into two parts:
   - runCompute(r, channel): crop the photo, build the fixed palette, call runWorker, unpack the result. It returns {key: computeKey(r), layout, layoutParams, data, palette, diagnostics, processed}.
   - commit(result): everything that is saved today, i.e. setRec with palette, diagnostics and computedWith, the thumbnail, saveProject, saveMosaic and saveProgress.
   compute() becomes commit(await runCompute(r, 'compute')).

2. Add a 'preview' channel to the Channel type in src/workers/client.ts. compute.worker.ts needs no change. Cancelling a stale preview with cancelChannel('preview') then never kills a real compute or a PDF job.

3. Add a preview state to useProject:
   - Watch computeKey(rec). Wait about 600 ms after the last change, cancel any running preview, then start runCompute(rec, 'preview').
   - Keep a request counter and drop results whose key no longer matches.
   - Start previews automatically only while cols*rows is at most about 250k AND the last preview took under about 2 s, since slow Android phones may be 3-5x slower than the desktop timings. Otherwise show a 'Vorschau aktualisieren' button.
   - Never write to IndexedDB. Never touch rec.palette, computedWith, computed or progress.

4. Add a new <LivePreview api> component:
   - Render preview.data with renderFull(layout, data, palette, ~640, {groutHex, surface, realistic: true}) into a canvas.
   - Show a small badge 'Vorschau – noch nicht übernommen', a spinner while the next preview runs, and a photo/mosaic toggle.
   - Make it the main right-hand visual in StepSize, StepTiles and StepJoint, with LayoutSummary as a compact stat strip below it.
   - In StepColors, put it above the palette editor. It may also show the preview palette as read-only swatches labelled as a preview.
   - In StepShapes, add it as a third view or a toggle next to the region editor. Do not replace the editor.

5. StepCompute becomes 'Übernehmen':
   - If preview.key === computeKey(rec), commit(preview) directly, with no second computation. Otherwise run the normal compute.
   - Keep the existing overwriteWarn. When api.computed already has manual edits or progress, ask for confirmation before overwriting.
   - Only when nothing has been computed yet (no api.computed) may the matching preview be committed automatically on entering step 8.
   - Never commit automatically over an existing mosaic, because that would destroy manual edits and laying progress.

6. Tests:
   - A unit test that runCompute output with the same key equals the committed data. The k-means seed is deterministic.
   - An e2e check that a canvas appears in step-tiles and changes when switching 4 mm to 8 mm, with no project write before 'Übernehmen'. For example, the computed badge and computedWith stay unchanged.

Add a live mosaic preview to steps 2-6 that never changes saved data, and make step 7 an explicit "Übernehmen" (commit).

1) Separate worker channel. In src/workers/client.ts extend Channel to 'compute' | 'stats' | 'pdf' | 'preview'. Before each new preview request call cancelChannel('preview'). This terminates a stale job immediately, so jobs never queue up, and cancelCompute() no longer affects previews (or the other way round). Reuse the existing 'compute' worker message type; no worker change is needed.

2) Add useProject.previewCompute(), a pure function with no side effects.
- Factor the input preparation of compute() (crop, workingSize, renderCropped, canvasToRaw, fixed palette; useProject.ts:280-302) into a shared helper.
- Cache the raw working image keyed by JSON {adjust, crop, ws}. Changes to colours, shapes or joint often keep the same ws, and then skip the main-thread resize.
- Store the result in preview state {key: computeKey(rec), lang, materialsRef, ws, layout, data, palette, diagnostics}.
- Never call setRec, setPalette, saveProject, saveMosaic or saveProgress, and never touch computedWith or the thumbnail.

3) Trigger with an adaptive limit instead of a fixed 250k.
- Debounce on computeKey(rec) changes: about 500 ms for chips and presets, about 800 ms for typed numbers.
- Run automatically only while cells are at most about 60k (about 30k when navigator.hardwareConcurrency is 4 or less, or on a coarse pointer), and only while the last preview took under about 1.5 s.
- Otherwise show a "Vorschau aktualisieren" button with an estimated duration.
- Measured basis: a 12 MP photo needs 0.95 s at 37k positions and 2.6 s at 214k on desktop.

4) Add a <LivePreview> component.
- Render with renderFull(layout, data, palette, ~640, {groutHex, surface, realistic: true}) and a before/after toggle (processed photo vs mosaic).
- Label it permanently "Vorschau – noch nicht übernommen".
- While a new preview is running, dim the old image and show a spinner, so an outdated picture never looks current.
- Under it, show a compact stat strip with the existing LayoutSummary values, which are exact geometry.
- Do not show per-colour stone counts or material needs from the preview. Those keep coming only from the committed stats worker.

5) Placement per step.
- StepSize, StepTiles, StepJoint: LivePreview on top of the right column, LayoutSummary condensed under it.
- StepColors: add a two-column layout with LivePreview plus a read-only strip of preview swatches (number + HEX). The editable PaletteEditor stays bound to the committed palette.
- StepShapes: keep RegionEditor and add a "Foto / Mosaik" toggle on the same canvas. Regions are normalised to effectiveCrop, the same frame as the mosaic, so the overlay lines up and the user sees the effect of face/detail regions.
- Below 980 px: make the preview a sticky, compact element (about 35vh) above the controls, so phone users see changes as they tap.

6) Commit rules (protecting progress and manual edits).
- Step 7 "Übernehmen": if the preview's key, lang, materials and ws equal the current values, persist the preview result directly through the same code as compute() (palette, diagnostics, computedWith, thumbnail, mosaic, progress). This is instant and identical to what the user saw, because k-means is seeded (mosaic.ts:441). Otherwise run compute() as today.
- Auto-commit on entering step 8 is allowed only when no mosaic exists yet (!rec.computedWith && !api.computed).
- If a committed mosaic exists and the settings differ, never auto-recompute. Show the preview as "neue Einstellungen" next to the stale badge. Require an explicit Übernehmen with the existing 'compute.overwriteWarn' plus the number of laid stones and manual edits that would be lost. compute() resets progress at useProject.ts:346.

7) Tests.
- Vitest: previewCompute leaves rec, palette, computedWith and the IndexedDB stores unchanged.
- Vitest: an adopted preview equals a fresh compute() byte for byte (colorIdx, shapes, pieces) for all four sample projects.
- E2E: changing the tile size in step 3 updates the mosaic-preview canvas without the step 7 compute button.
- E2E: a project with laid stones keeps its progress after visiting steps 2-6 with live preview.

Effort: M (closer to M/L with the image cache and the mobile layout). Impact: 5.

kept.title: Default first result for an uploaded portrait is unrecognizable (30 cm / 8 mm = 34 columns), with no guidance on detail level
kept.problem: A user who uploads a real portrait and clicks 'Weiter' through the steps gets 34 × 41 stones. The eyes are about one stone each and the face cannot be recognized. Nothing tells them that tile size relative to width decides whether a face is readable. Automatic face detection is unavailable in Chromium, so the face-protection features stay unused unless the user discovers the region tool by themselves.
kept.evidence: Real public-domain portrait (Gilbert Stuart's Washington, Wikimedia thumbnail) in dl/washington.jpg, uploaded through home-photo with the defaults. /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/ux-desktop/journey4.out: 'Raster 34 × 41, 1.394 positions'; 'face detect message: Automatische Gesichtserkennung wird von diesem Browser nicht unterstützt'. Side by side: compare-defaults.png (default vs 30cm/4mm vs 60cm/5mm) and shots/j4-02-default-result.png. Defaults: src/core/types.ts:191-201 (widthMm 300, tileW 8, colorCount 24). The bundled portrait sample uses 400 mm / 5 mm, i.e. 67 columns (src/ui/Home.tsx SAMPLES).

N Steine über die Gesichtsbreite' (region.w × cols) with a hint below about 20. 2) In Home.newProject() and useProject.setPhoto(), suggest a tile size from the 2-12 mm presets that gives about 70-90 columns for the chosen width, or change DEFAULT_SETTINGS to 400 mm / 5 mm. Show it as a dismissible suggestion, not a silent change. 3) In StepShapes, when detectFaces() returns null, hide 'Gesichter erkennen' and show a prominent card: 'Ist ein Gesicht im Bild? kept.title: Ghost click on touch: tapping a stone opens the dialog, then the same tap marks the stone as laid or switches to a neighbour stone
kept.problem: On touch devices the Viewer opens the stone dialog on pointerup (Viewer.tsx:215-241, onPick). The browser then sends the compatibility mousedown/mouseup/click for the same tap to whatever element of the new modal is under the finger. The user only wanted to look at a stone, but the stray click can tick 'dieser Stein ist verlegt' (laying progress is written and saved) or press a neighbour button so the dialog shows a different stone. This breaks requirement 13 (inspect a stone) and requirement 14 (correct progress), and the user never sees it happen.
kept.evidence: Reproduction (Playwright, 390x844, hasTouch). /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/ux-mobile-android/scripts/ghost.cjs taps a stone twice: once with the ghost events suppressed (reference) and once as a normal tap. Output in .../out/ghost.txt: {"y":519,"tapped":"AK034","shown":"AK035",ghostClick:"click->span.muted rechts"}, {"y":544,"tapped":"AP034","shown":"AP033-1",ghostClick:"click->button.neighbor links AP033"}. Variant .../scripts/ghost2.cjs (.../out/ghost2.txt): {"y":360,"tapped":"B022","placedAfter":true,"ghostClick":"click->label.inline dieser Stein ist verlegt"}. Afterwards the plan step shows 'placed-count after only opening dialogs in preview: 1'. The event log in .../out/touch.txt shows 'pointerup:canvas' followed by 'mousedown/mouseup/click:button.neighbor' at the same coordinates. Related code: components.tsx:115 (backdrop closes on onMouseDown) and StoneDialog.tsx:155-166 (placed checkbox inside a label).
kept.proposal: 1) Viewer.tsx: for e.pointerType !== 'mouse', do not call onPick in onUp. Store the pending pick and run it from a 'click' listener on the canvas; the click still lands on the canvas because the modal does not exist yet. Alternatively, add a non-passive canvas 'touchend' listener that calls e.preventDefault() after a recognised tap, which suppresses the synthetic mouse events. 2) Modal: close the backdrop on 'click' only when pointerdown also started on the backdrop, and ignore clicks in the first 350 ms after mount. 3) Add an e2e check with hasTouch: tap a stone, then assert placed-count is still 0 and stone-id equals the reference id.
corrected:
1) Viewer.tsx, root-cause fix, verified by injection. In the interaction useEffect, add `let tapHandled = false;`. In onUp, set `tapHandled = e.pointerType !== 'mouse'` right before calling `propsRef.current.onPick?.(...)`. Add `const onTouchEnd = (e: TouchEvent) => { if (tapHandled && e.cancelable) e.preventDefault(); tapHandled = false; };` and register it with `cv.addEventListener('touchend', onTouchEnd, { passive: false })`, removing it in the cleanup. pointerup fires before touchend, so the flag is set in time. preventDefault on touchend cancels the gesture tap, so no mousedown/mouseup/click reaches the new modal. Pan and pinch are unaffected because onPick is only called when !moved. The zoom buttons are separate elements and still work. A second option also works: defer onPick to a canvas 'click' listener when pointerType is not 'mouse'. The touchend variant is the one I tested.
2) components.tsx:115, defensive. Close the backdrop on click only if pointerdown also started on the backdrop. Use `onPointerDown={e => downOnBackdrop.current = e.target === e.currentTarget}` together with `onClick={e => { if (downOnBackdrop.current && e.target === e.currentTarget) props.onClose(); downOnBackdrop.current = false; }}`. This replaces the current onMouseDown close, so a stray mousedown cannot close a dialog on tablets where the backdrop lies under the finger. A 350 ms 'ignore clicks after mount' timer is not needed once step 1 is in place.
3) e2e/run-e2e.cjs. Add a hasTouch/isMobile context, then use page.touchscreen.tap at several canvas points that previously hit the placed row and the neighbour buttons (e.g. x=140, y=360 and y=540 on a 390x844 viewport after compute on the portrait sample). After each tap, assert that [data-testid=stone-placed] is unchecked and that stone-id equals the id from a reference tap with mouse events suppressed. At the end, assert placed-count is 0 in the plan step.

1) src/ui/project/Viewer.tsx, in the interaction useEffect:
(a) Separate the cancel handler from onUp. A 'pointercancel' should only remove the pointer and reset downAt, moved and pinchDist. It must never call onPick. Today onUp is registered for pointercancel at line 283.
(b) Keep a flag `tapPicked` and set it to true in onUp when a touch tap is recognised: e.pointerType === 'touch', pointers.size === 0, downAt is set and moved is false. Then register `cv.addEventListener('touchend', (e) => { if (tapPicked) { e.preventDefault(); tapPicked = false; } }, { passive: false })` and remove it in the cleanup function. This stops Chromium/Android WebView from sending the synthetic mousedown/mouseup/click into the modal that has just opened. kept.title: Android back button leaves the app from every screen, including open dialogs; in the PWA, back jumps from step 8 to Home
kept.problem: The APK does not include @capacitor/app (package.json; capacitor.plugins.json lists only filesystem and share). Capacitor 8's BridgeActivity has no back handling: there is no OnBackPressedCallback anywhere in @capacitor/android. So the hardware back button or back gesture takes the default Activity path. On Android 12 and newer it sends the app to the background; on Android 7-11 it finishes the activity, which destroys the WebView and restarts the app on Home. Back never closes a dialog and never returns to the previous step. In the browser/PWA, step changes use history.replaceState (Workspace.tsx:23-26) and modals are not in the history, so back always leaves the whole project. Pending saves depend only on visibilitychange/pagehide (useProject.ts:131-141); there is no native pause hook.
kept.evidence: Code: android/app/src/main/java/de/mosaicplan/app/MainActivity.java is an empty BridgeActivity. node_modules/@capacitor/android/.../BridgeActivity.java has no onBackPressed, and grep for OnBackPressed or canGoBack finds only MockCordovaWebViewImpl. android/app/src/main/assets/capacitor.plugins.json contains only Filesystem and Share. Browser reproduction: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/ux-mobile-android/scripts/back.cjs opens a project, computes it, goes to step 8, opens a stone dialog and presses back. Output (.../out/back.txt): 'after BACK #1: http://localhost:4173/ | dialog still open: false | on home: true'. history.length stays 3 across step changes.
kept.proposal: Add @capacitor/app (npx cap sync). Create a small back-handler stack, src/ui/backStack.ts, with a LIFO list and a useBackHandler(fn, active) hook. Modal registers onClose while mounted. Workspace registers 'go to previous step' when idx > 0, and 'go to project list' at step 1. App registers 'go to #/' when route !== ''. In main.tsx, when isNative(): App.addListener('backButton', () => { if (!backStack.run()) App.minimizeApp(); }). Use minimizeApp rather than exitApp so state survives. Also App.addListener('pause', () => flushAll()), where useProject registers its flush in a global set. For the web/PWA: use history.pushState for step changes instead of replaceState, push a {modal} entry when a Modal opens, and close it on popstate. Add an e2e check that page.goBack() with an open dialog only closes the dialog.
corrected:
Use browser history as the single source of truth for both the PWA and the APK.

(1) Workspace: make the step come from the route.
- In Workspace.tsx, replace the `useState` step with a value derived from the route: `const step = isStep(initialStep) ? initialStep : 'photo'`.
- Change `setStep(s)` to `location.hash = '#/project/' + id + '/' + s`. This pushes a history entry, and App's existing hashchange listener re-renders Workspace with the new `initialStep`. Workspace stays mounted because `key` is the project id, so the project is not reloaded.
- Use `history.replaceState` plus a `setHash` call only for the automatic jump to 'preview' after loading (Workspace.tsx:28-31), so that it does not create an extra entry.

(2) Modal (components.tsx:107): give it its own history entry.
- On mount, run once: `history.pushState({ mpModal: true }, '')` (same URL, so no hashchange fires).
- Add a `popstate` listener that calls `onCloseRef.current()`. Keep `onClose` in a ref so the effect does not re-run on every render; the current effect depends on `[props]`.
- When the modal closes through ✕, Escape or the backdrop, call `history.back()` if `history.state?.mpModal` is set, and ignore the resulting popstate.
- Guard against the StrictMode double mount by checking `history.state?.mpModal` before pushing.

(3) Native app:
- `npm i @capacitor/app@^8.1` and `npx cap sync android`.
- In main.tsx, when `isNative()`, add: `App.addListener('backButton', ({ canGoBack }) => canGoBack ? history.back() : App.minimizeApp())`. Hash and pushState entries count in the WebView's canGoBack. Use `minimizeApp`, not `exitApp`, so in-memory state survives.
- Optional hardening: `App.addListener('pause', () => flushAllProjects())`, where useProject registers its `flush` in a module-level Set.

(4) Add e2e checks in e2e/run-e2e.cjs:
- (a) With the stone dialog open, `page.goBack()` closes the dialog, the URL stays on `.../preview`, and the canvas is still visible.
- (b) Going from colors to preview and then `goBack()` shows step 'colors' (the active stepper button and the h2).
- (c) A further `goBack()` leaves the project only after the step history is used up.

Impact 4, effort M.

Use one back mechanism: browser history, the same on web and Android.

(1) Steps controlled by the URL, in Workspace.tsx:
- Add useEffect(() => { if (STEPS.includes(initialStep) && initialStep !== step) setStep(initialStep) }, [initialStep]) so a back or forward traversal updates the screen.
- Make user clicks on the stepper, the Next/Back buttons and the stale badge call goStep(s), which pushes the new hash (location.hash = h, or history.pushState plus setStep).
- Keep replaceState for automatic redirects only, for example the 'preview' jump after loading at Workspace.tsx:28-31, so back never lands on a step the user did not choose.

(2) Modals in history, in components.tsx Modal:
- On mount, run history.pushState({mpModal: id}, '') with the same URL.
- Listen for popstate. When this modal's entry is no longer current, call onClose.
- Have the X button, Escape and a backdrop tap call history.back() instead of onClose; the popstate handler then closes the modal.
- In the cleanup, if the modal unmounts programmatically (for example after Save) and history.state?.mpModal === id, call history.back() so no stale entry is left.
- Keep a module-level depth counter so the nested free-form modal in StoneDialog closes first.

(3) Android:
- Add @capacitor/app@^8.1 (8.1.2 exists, peer @capacitor/core >=8) and run npx cap sync.
- In main.tsx, when isNative(): App.addListener('backButton', ({canGoBack}) => canGoBack ? history.back() : App.minimizeApp()).
- Do not use exitApp, and do not build a separate JS backStack.
- The listener is mandatory: without it, plugin 8.1.2 ignores back at the root.
- Optional: App.addListener('pause', flushAll), where useProject registers its flush in a module-level Set.

(4) Tests: extend e2e/run-e2e.cjs:
- Open the stone dialog, call page.goBack(), and check that the dialog is closed and the URL and active step-* are unchanged.
- Call goBack() again and check that the previous step is shown and the active stepper button matches the URL hash.
- Open the nested free-form modal and check that back closes only the inner modal.
- Check manually on a device or emulator with API 30 and API 34+ that back at Home minimizes the app and that reopening keeps the state.

No changes to src/core, so stone counts and cut dimensions are not affected. Impact 4 (5 on Android 7-11), effort M.

kept.title: Laying mode and stone taps at overview zoom hit random stones (about 6 px per stone); taps 4 px apart lay three different stones and there is no undo
kept.problem: The plan step opens fitted to the screen. On a phone the 30x40 cm portrait sample is drawn at about 1 CSS px per mm, so one 5 mm stone plus joint is about 6 CSS px, roughly 1 mm on the physical screen. A fingertip covers dozens of stones. In laying mode every tap without movement toggles whatever stone lies under the touch point. A finger offset of 4 px already lays a different stone. At this zoom nothing visible changes, so the user does not notice, and README states there is no undo. The tap slop is 5 px (Viewer.tsx:201), smaller than typical finger jitter, and long presses also count as taps (downAt.t is never used). The preview has the same problem: taps 3 px apart open different stones.
kept.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/ux-mobile-android/scripts/touch.cjs (output .../out/touch.txt): 'lay mode placed after taps at (0,0),(+4,0),(0,+4) px: 1 2 3' and 'stone ids for taps at +0,+3,+6 px: [AP033-1, AP034, AP034]'. Screenshot .../shots/m-touch.png (right panel): 3 stones marked as laid, with no visible marker at fit zoom. Canvas size 340x523 CSS px for 300x400 mm. Code: StepPlan.tsx:120-126 (togglePiecePlaced on every pick), Viewer.tsx:196-244.

Instead animate a zoom centred on the tap point to the scale where a stone is about 36 px, and show the hint 'Zum Verlegen hineinzoomen'. Raise the touch tap slop to 10 px and ignore presses longer than 500 ms. After each toggle in laying mode, flash the stone outline for 400 ms and call navigator.vibrate?.(10). In StepPlan, keep the last 50 toggles as {idx, piece, prevBit} and add a 'Rückgängig' button next to the laying-mode toggle. Then compute its on-screen size: min(layout.colW[col], layout.rowH[row]) * view.scale for a full cell, or the bbox of the target piece's polygon for split or cut cells. If that size is under about 24 CSS px, do not call onPick. Instead animate a zoom (about 200 ms) centred on the tap point, up to the scale where that cell is about 40 px, capped at maxS. 2) Touch slop: raise it to 10 px for touch (keep 5 px for mouse). Treat a press longer than 500 ms as 'not a tap' (do not call onPick). Do not treat pointercancel as a tap: register a separate handler that only clears state.
3) StepPlan.tsx: keep an undo stack in state, capped at 50 entries. A single toggle pushes {idx, piece}; undo XORs the same bit again (togglePiecePlaced is an XOR, edits.ts:127). The section 'complete' and 'reset' actions push a copy of data.progress for that section's row/col range, restored with a small edits.ts helper. Show a 'Rückgängig (n)' button next to the 'Verlegemodus' toggle, plus a status line naming the last change, e.g. 'AP034 als verlegt markiert' / 'AP034 wieder offen' (use pieceId from layout.ts:184). 5) Optional: a row mode. In lay mode, a 'Reihe' segmented option marks every stone from the tapped cell to the end of that row within the selected section, pushing a single undo entry.

1. Viewer.tsx, onDown, onMove and onUp: store e.pointerType at pointer-down.
   - For touch and pen, use a tap slop of 10 px; keep 5 px for the mouse.

Call the existing zoomAt(p.x, p.y, k) with k chosen so that this stone becomes about 40 px (zoomAt already respects maxS = 120). Show a short hint, "Zum Antippen hineingezoomt" / "Zoomed in so you can tap a single stone" / tr equivalent.

   - A tap at fit zoom in laying mode leaves placed-count unchanged and increases the zoom.

   - "Abschnitt fertig" followed by "Rückgängig" restores the earlier count exactly, including partly laid sections.

Leave the row-by-row mode for a separate follow-up, such as "Bereich aufziehen = verlegt" using setRangePlaced, which already counts exactly.

kept.title: APK file saving gives no feedback and fails silently on Android 10; after the share sheet the user cannot find or reopen the PDF/CSV/backup
kept.problem: saveNative (platform.ts:20-36) tries Directory.Documents and silently swallows any failure. It returns savedPath, but downloadBlob ignores it (components.tsx:157-160). Callers do not await it (StepPdf.tsx:73, StepPlan.tsx:48, Projects.tsx:76), so errors become unhandled rejections. On native the 'Öffnen' link is hidden (StepPdf.tsx:182), and the only message is 'PDF erstellt (x KB).' The Filesystem plugin's own README says Directory.Documents on Android 10 and older needs READ+WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE. The manifest declares only WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE with maxSdkVersion=28, no READ, and no requestLegacyExternalStorage, so on Android 10 (API 29) the Documents write is rejected and only the share sheet remains. If the user dismisses it, the file exists only in the app cache. This matters especially for project export, which README names as the only protection against data loss when reinstalling.
kept.evidence: Code: src/platform.ts:22-27 (try writeFile Documents, catch {}), src/ui/components.tsx:158-160 ('await saveNative(blob, name); return;' with the result unused), android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml (only WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE maxSdkVersion=28), node_modules/@capacitor/filesystem/README.md lines 114-123 ('in Android 10 and older, this API requires ... READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE ... WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE'), and FilesystemPlugin.kt:408-416 (below API 30 it requires the PUBLIC_STORAGE alias = READ+WRITE). The i18n string 'pdfui.done' (de.ts:402) gives no location. Not testable on a device here; the conclusion comes from the plugin source and docs.
kept.proposal: 1) Make downloadBlob return {savedPath, shared, error} and await it everywhere. Show an inline success line or toast: 'Gespeichert: Dokumente/MosaicPlan/<name>' or 'Konnte nicht in Dokumente speichern – bitte über Teilen sichern'. 2) On native, replace the hidden 'Öffnen' link with 'Erneut teilen/öffnen', which calls Share.share({files:[cacheUri]}) again. 3) Quick manifest fix: WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE with maxSdkVersion="29" plus android:requestLegacyExternalStorage="true" on <application>. 4) Robust option: a ~40-line custom plugin in MainActivity that opens Intent.ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT (system 'Speichern unter' dialog, no permissions needed on API 24-36) and writes the bytes to the returned Uri. Use it for 'Projekt sichern' and 'PDF speichern'.
corrected:
1) src/platform.ts: make saveNative return `{ savedPath: string; cacheUri: string; shared: boolean; error?: string }`.
- Record the Documents writeFile error message instead of using an empty catch.
- Treat Share's 'Share canceled' rejection as shared=false, not as an error.
- Let real failures (blobToBase64, Cache write) propagate.

2) src/ui/components.tsx:157: make downloadBlob return that result; on the web return `{ savedPath: '', shared: false }`. Await it at all four call sites: StepPdf.tsx:73, StepPlan.tsx:48, Projects.tsx:76 and Materials.tsx:114, the last one missing from the original finding. Wrap each call in try/catch that shows the error.
- In StepPdf, call setResult only after the save resolves.
- On native, show one of two messages:
  - 'Gespeichert: Dokumente/MosaicPlan/<name>' when savedPath is set.
  - A warning badge 'Nicht in Dokumente gespeichert – bitte über Teilen sichern (<reason>)' when it is not.
- Add i18n keys in de/en/tr.

3) Replace the hidden 'Öffnen' link (StepPdf.tsx:182) with an 'Erneut teilen' button that calls Share.share({ files: [cacheUri] }). Use the same button for the CSV and project export messages.
- Projects.tsx export also needs a visible confirmation. It currently has none.
- Optionally add a timestamp to the backup file name so an older backup is not silently overwritten.

4) AndroidManifest.xml quick fix: declare WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, both with maxSdkVersion="29", and set android:requestLegacyExternalStorage="true" on <application>.
- Android 7-10 will then show a storage permission prompt on the first export. Point 2 must handle a denial with the warning message.
- On API 30+ the plugin does not request permissions for Directory.Documents writes (isStoragePermissionGranted(false) returns true), so the maxSdkVersion cap is safe for the app's current calls.

5) Robust option for 'Projekt sichern' and 'PDF speichern': a small custom Capacitor plugin (Java, registered in MainActivity via registerPlugin(SaveAsPlugin.class) before super.onCreate).
- It launches Intent.ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT with the right MIME type and suggested name. This is the system 'Speichern unter' dialog and needs no permissions on API 24-36.
- In the activity result it stream-copies the already-written cache file (cacheUri from point 1) into the returned content Uri via ContentResolver.openOutputStream. Do not pass the base64 payload over the bridge a second time, which matters for large PDFs.
- Return the chosen display name so the UI can confirm where the file was saved.

1) Report the real outcome of every save (src/platform.ts, src/ui/components.tsx):
- Change saveNative to return `{ savedPath: string | null, cacheUri: string, shared: boolean, error?: string }`. Set `savedPath` only when Filesystem.writeFile to Documents actually resolved. On failure, keep the error message. Set `shared` from the Share.share result (it rejects when dismissed).
- downloadBlob returns `Promise<SaveResult>` (on the web: `{ kind: 'download' }`).

2) Await the save in all four callers, inside their existing try/catch: StepPdf.tsx:73, StepPlan.tsx:48, Projects.tsx:76 and Materials.tsx:114. A failure then shows up as an error instead of an unhandled rejection under a success message.

3) Add a small shared status line component (role="status", aria-live="polite") in components.tsx. New i18n keys in de, en and tr:
- Success: "Gespeichert: Dokumente/MosaicPlan/<name>". Show it only when `savedPath` is set; never claim a location that was not written.
- Failure: "Nicht in Dokumente gespeichert (<Grund>). Bitte über Teilen sichern." plus a "Teilen" button.

4) On native, replace the hidden "Öffnen" link (StepPdf.tsx:182) with a "Teilen / Öffnen" button. Keep `cacheUri` in component state and call Share.share({ files: [cacheUri] }) again. Do the same after project export in Projects.tsx.

5) Avoid name collisions on native. Add a timestamp suffix to exported file names, e.g. `<name>_2026-11-07_1432.mosaicplan.json` and `_verlegeplan_<ts>.pdf`. If writeFile still fails, retry once with a `_2` suffix. Without this, a backup written after a reinstall on Android 11+ fails silently because the old file belongs to the previous installation.

6) Manifest fix for Android 10 (android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml), as required by the Filesystem plugin README and FilesystemPlugin.kt:410-416:
- `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE" android:maxSdkVersion="29"/>`
- Change WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE to maxSdkVersion="29".
- Add `android:requestLegacyExternalStorage="true"` on `<application>`. Android 10 honours this flag regardless of targetSdk 36; Android 11+ ignores it, where it is not needed.
Android 7-10 users then get one storage prompt. If they refuse, step 3 shows the share fallback.

7) Optional, later: a small Capacitor plugin in MainActivity using Intent.ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT (the system "Speichern unter" dialog, no permissions needed) for "Projekt sichern" and "PDF speichern". Write the bytes in chunks instead of one large base64 string, so big section PDFs do not have to cross the bridge in one piece.

8) Verification and honesty:
- Add a vitest test that mocks platform.ts and checks that downloadBlob reports `savedPath` = null when writeFile rejects, and that the UI then shows the failure message, not a path.
- Add a README line saying the Android save behaviour has only been checked from source until it is tested on Android 10 and 13+.

kept.title: A full-resolution photo bitmap stays in memory for the whole session: a 48 MP phone photo costs about +285 MB, a crash risk in Android WebView
kept.problem: loadBitmap (imagePrep.ts:10-16) decodes the original at full resolution, and useProject keeps that ImageBitmap in state for the lifetime of the project (useProject.ts:73-81, 186-197). The app never needs more than workingSize (max 6 MP, imagePrep.ts:128-133), and the crop preview is 900 px wide. ImageBitmap.close() is never called anywhere, so replaced photos are freed only when GC runs. Modern phones produce 48-200 MP photos, and the WebView renderer on mid-range Android devices is memory-limited.
kept.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/ux-mobile-android/scripts/bigphoto.cjs measures the RSS of the Chromium process tree (phone emulation) when loading a photo through home-photo and then computing. 3 MP: 'chromium tree RSS 459 MB -> 520 MB (+61 MB)', peak 595 MB. 48 MP (8000x6000, .../img/photo48mp.jpg): 'RSS 461 MB -> 746 MB (+285 MB)', 'peak during compute 807 MB'. The crop canvas is only 900x675 in both cases. grep for '.close()' in src/ui and src/workers finds no bitmap close.
kept.proposal: In loadBitmap, first read the dimensions (createImageBitmap(blob) and close it, or decode the header), then decode again with { imageOrientation: 'from-image', resizeWidth/resizeHeight such that the long side is at most 4096 px, resizeQuality: 'high' }. That is enough for 6 MP working size plus crop headroom and caps memory at about 64 MB. Call prev.close() in setPhoto and in the useProject unmount cleanup. Optionally store a downscaled JPEG (long side 4096, q 0.92) next to the original and use only that in the app. Add a note in the photo step when the source was reduced.
corrected:
1. Change src/ui/project/imagePrep.ts loadBitmap so it returns `{ bitmap, srcW, srcH }` and never decodes at full size just to learn the dimensions:
   - Read the size from the header: create an object URL, load it into an `Image` and wait for `onload` (do not use `img.decode()`), take naturalWidth/naturalHeight (these already respect EXIF), then revoke the URL.
   - If srcW*srcH > MAX_PX (about 16e6, which is about 64 MB of RGBA), call `createImageBitmap(blob, { imageOrientation: 'from-image', resizeWidth: round(srcW*s), resizeHeight: round(srcH*s), resizeQuality: 'high' })` with `s = sqrt(MAX_PX/(srcW*srcH))`. Otherwise keep today's call. Keep today's code as the fallback if anything throws.
   - A limit on pixel area keeps crop room for workingSize (6 MP) and keeps panoramas usable, which a 4096 px long-side limit does not.
2. Fix src/ui/Home.tsx:29 and :44. They decode a full bitmap only to compute the aspect ratio and never release it. Use the header-only size read there, or call `b.close()` right after reading width and height. Closing alone lowered the measured load peak from about 840-880 to about 745 MB.
3. In src/ui/project/useProject.ts, release replaced or unmounted bitmaps with `useEffect(() => () => { bitmap?.close(); }, [bitmap])` instead of closing `prev` inside setPhoto. That way a pending render (StepPhoto or StepShapes) or effect cannot use a bitmap that is already closed. compute() uses the bitmap synchronously before it awaits the worker, so it is safe either way.
4. In src/ui/project/StepPhoto.tsx:104, show the original and the working size when the photo was reduced, for example "8000 × 6000 px (bearbeitet mit 4618 × 3464 px)". Add the strings in de, en and tr.
5. Expect, as measured: about 110 MB less memory at rest and at the compute peak for a 48 MP photo. The load peak stays high because Chromium still decodes at full size before resizing. Photos at or below 16 MP, which includes the default 12 MP phone photo, are unchanged.
6. Add an e2e check: upload an 8000x6000 JPEG and assert that the displayed working size is at most MAX_PX. Upload an image with EXIF orientation 6 and assert that it stays portrait with the correct corner on top (resize applies to the oriented dimensions in Chromium 153). Rate impact 2-3, effort S.

Use a capped bitmap for working in the project, but compute from the full image when needed. The mosaic result stays identical to today, so geometry, counts and cut dimensions are untouched.

1. imagePrep.ts: add loadWorkingBitmap(blob, maxSide = 4096). It returns { bmp, origW, origH, reduced }.
   - Decode once with { imageOrientation: 'from-image' } and read origW and origH.
   - If max(origW, origH) > maxSide:
     - Close that bitmap.
     - Decode again with resizeWidth and resizeHeight set from ONE uniform scale factor, plus resizeQuality 'high'.
     - Check that |bmp.width/bmp.height - origW/origH| < 0.5%. If the check fails, or the call throws, fall back to the full decode (protection for old WebViews).
   - This order measured the lowest peak.
   - Keep loadBitmap for the full-resolution path.

2. useProject.ts: use the new loader at both decode sites, :79 (opening a project) and :188 (new photo). Store origW and origH in state.
   - effectiveCrop and the aspect calculation can keep using the capped bitmap, because both only need the aspect ratio.
   - In compute():
     - Compute rw and rh from origW and origH via rotatedSize, and compute ws with workingSize exactly as today (sourcePx = crop.w*rw*crop.h*rh).
     - If the crop at capped resolution has fewer pixels than ws.w*ws.h, decode a temporary full bitmap from image.original. Otherwise use the capped bitmap.
     - Call renderCropped, then close the temporary bitmap in a finally block.
   - The working image then has the same pixel count as today. Compare the hashes of the old and new raw.data for the four sample projects and a 48 MP photo.

3. Home.tsx:29 and :44: call b.close() right after reading the aspect ratio. These are full-resolution decodes that are never released today.

4. Release bitmaps through the React lifecycle, not inside setPhoto. In useProject, add `useEffect(() => () => { bitmap?.close(); }, [bitmap]);`.
   - Cleanups run after child effects such as StepPhoto's 180 ms timer have been cleared, which avoids drawImage on a detached bitmap.
   - With StrictMode, the double-invoke at mount happens while bitmap is still null, so it is harmless.

5. StepPhoto.tsx:104: show the original size, plus a note when the image was reduced, e.g. "8000 × 6000 px (for editing reduced to 4096 × 3072; the calculation uses full resolution)". Add the string to i18n de/en/tr.

6. Do not claim it fixes the load-time memory peak: createImageBitmap's resize still decodes at full resolution. If the peak itself turns out to crash on a device, a follow-up would be to decode in a worker or in strips. That should be measured on a real Android device before it is promised.

7. Tests:
   - e2e: upload the 48 MP JPEG and assert that the crop canvas and the mosaic-canvas appear.
   - unit or e2e: an EXIF orientation 6 photo keeps portrait orientation after the capped decode.
   - Assert the identical working-image size before and after the change for a 1000x750 cm project with a 10% crop.

1. Move parsing into a pure module, src/ui/numberParse.ts (no React import), so vitest in tests/ can import it. Use `parseLocaleNum(s, lang)`:
   (a) Remove all whitespace, including U+00A0, U+2009 and U+202F.
   (b) Pick the separators per language: for de/tr, group = '.' and decimal = ','; for en, group = ',' and decimal = '.'.
   (c) If the text matches `^-?[1-9]\d{0,2}(G\d{3})+(D\d*)?$` (G = escaped group char, D = escaped decimal char), remove all G characters and turn D into '.'. The leading [1-9] stops '0.125' from being read as thousands.

For 'custom' and 'materials', keep every entry in its input order with its input code and only map indices; unused colours show 0 stones. kept.title: Freeform validation accepts overlapping stones and stones with no joint; joint area can go negative
kept.problem: validateFreePieces relies on polygonsOverlap, which only detects strictly crossing edges (segIntersect excludes collinear and endpoint contacts) plus a centroid-in-polygon test. Overlaps where edges are collinear or vertices lie on edges are missed, which is typical when drawing on the editor's 0.1 mm grid. The function also never checks that pieces are at least one joint apart, so stones can touch. The overlap is then counted twice: stoneArea becomes larger than the finished area and jointArea goes negative. The invariant 'Steinfläche + Fugenfläche = Gesamtfläche' cannot catch this because stats.ts defines jointArea = finishedArea - stoneArea, so it holds by construction.

kept.title: Raw-stone count is too optimistic: fractional yields of different cut shapes are added up before rounding
kept.problem: computeStats adds 1/yieldPerRaw for every piece of a colour regardless of shape, then rounds up once per colour. A strip with yield 2 and a triangle with yield 2 count as 1 raw stone together, even when they cannot come from the same raw stone. Waste uses the same unrounded raw area, so waste % does not match the displayed raw count. Rectangle yield also has no cutting allowance (kerf/breakage) and uses DIM_TOL in the floor, e.g. two 4.02 mm pieces from an 8.00 mm tile.
kept.evidence: src/core/stats.ts:190-192 (rawExact += 1/yield; rawArea += y*w*h), :211 (single ceil per colour), :243-244 (waste from fractional rawArea); src/core/pieces.ts:265-267. Repro /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-core/r6_yield_mixing.out: 'Blau piece in col 0: triangle 7.29x7.29 yieldPerRaw=2', 'Blau piece in col 2: rectangle 3.50x8.00 yieldPerRaw=2', 'computeStats Blau: pieces=2 rawExact=1 raw=1'. Two raw stones are physically required: the triangle's minimum width is 5.15 mm, but only 4.5 mm remains next to the strip. On 24 sample runs (t3_pipeline.out) the app's rawTotal is below a count that never shares raw stones across shape/size groups (an upper bound) by 8-48 stones, e.g. cfg3 animal 327 vs 352 (7%) and cfg0 animal 1602 vs 1650.
kept.proposal: In computeStats, accumulate counts per (colour, cutInfo.signature or shape|w|h|yield) in a Map. After the loop, set raw per colour = sum over groups of ceil(n / yield) and rawArea = sum of raw * rawW * rawH. Waste then matches the rounded count. Add a `cutLossMm` setting (default about 0.5 mm) and use floor((W + loss) / (w + loss)) for rectangle yield, without DIM_TOL. Update README section 'Materialbedarf'. Turn the r6 scenario into a unit test expecting 2.
corrected:
If anything is done, keep it small and honest:
(1) In computeStats, after per-colour rounding, compute rawArea = sum over colours of cs.raw * cs.rawW * cs.rawH. That makes wasteArea and wastePct match the displayed raw count (stats.ts:243-244).
(2) Optional: keep a per-colour Map keyed by `${shape}|${w.toFixed(1)}|${h.toFixed(1)}|${yieldPerRaw}` (not cutInfo.signature, which splits identical shapes placed differently). Show it only as a "conservative upper bound" next to the current figure, or use it only for the stock-shortage warning (StepPlan.tsx:419). Do not replace the main count with it.
(3) Do not add a default cutting allowance. If a cutting allowance is added, make it an opt-in setting with default 0, so tile halves keep yield 2.
(4) In README 'Materialbedarf', state that the raw-tile count is an estimate based on per-shape yields: leftover pieces of different shapes are added up per colour, and the reserve covers the uncertainty.
(5) Add a unit test for the r6 scenario that checks rawWithReserve covers 2 at 10 % reserve, and that wastePct matches the rounded count.

In computeStats (src/core/stats.ts), stop adding 1/yieldPerRaw per piece. Instead:

(a) In the loop, keep one Map<CutInfo, number> per colour, keyed by object identity, so no string is built per piece. pieceCutInfo already returns cached CutInfo objects. After the loop, merge entries using a rotation-canonical key, computed once per unique CutInfo and memoised in a WeakMap: shape | rawW x rawH | yieldPerRaw | the vertex list of polyInRaw, translated to its bbox origin, rounded to 0.1 mm and sorted, taking the smallest string over 0/90/180/270° rotations. Do not mirror, because glass tiles have a face side. Then set cs.raw = Σ_groups ceil(n / yield), cs.rawWithReserve = ceil(cs.raw * (1 + reserve/100) - 1e-9), and rawArea = Σ_colours cs.raw * rawW * rawH. Waste and waste % then match the displayed count. Keep cs.rawExact only as the lower bound, or drop it.

(b) Label the number honestly in the UI, PDF and README ('Materialbedarf'). It is a safe upper bound: identical cuts (same shape, rotation allowed) share raw stones, but different cut shapes are counted separately. Leftover-piece reuse is not counted, and the reserve covers breakage.

(c) Optionally add a 'Schnittzugabe' (cut allowance) setting with default 0 mm, so today's yields stay the same. When it is set, compute rectangle yield as floor((W + loss + DIM_TOL) / (w + loss)). Keep DIM_TOL, to stay consistent with the fit check in pieces.ts:253 and to avoid floating-point mis-rounding.

(d) Optional follow-up (M): first-fit-decreasing packing of full-height rectangle strips of different widths in the same colour, e.g. 3.5 + 4.0 from 8 mm. This tightens the bound without ever going below what is physically possible.

Tests (tests/core.test.ts):
- r6 scenario: strip + diagonal triangle gives 2 Blau.
- One DIAG_A cell with both halves in one colour gives 1.
- Three isosceles diagonal triangles on 8x8 give 2.
- On 6x10: one DIAG_A cell with both halves Blau plus one mirrored DIAG_B half in Blau gives 2 Blau.
- The existing 256-whole-stones test is unchanged (256 / 282).
- Sections: Σ section raw ≥ total raw.

kept.title: NearestColorMatcher.nearestExact is not exact: CIE76 top-6 prefilter can drop the CIEDE2000 nearest colour
kept.problem: nearestExact keeps only the 6 CIE76-nearest palette colours and picks the best of those by CIEDE2000. CIE76 and CIEDE2000 rank saturated and dark colours very differently, so with sparse palettes (owned materials, few colours) the true CIEDE2000 optimum can be excluded. The method is also used for removePaletteColor's 'nearest remaining colour' and for dithering. In realistic k-means palettes the effect is small; the 0.5-unit cache adds roughly 0.3 dE.
kept.evidence: src/core/color.ts:229-262 (K = 6 prefilter) and :216-227 (0.5-unit cache). /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-core/t4_matcher.out: random palettes of 8/64/200 colours give 3.1%/4.8%/4.8% mismatches against brute-force CIEDE2000, worst +29.7 dE. t4c_worst.out: query #043956 -> chosen #90B4EC (dE2000 49.5) instead of #1755F5 (dE2000 19.9, which is CIE76 rank 7 of 8). Realistic cases: t4d_materials.out (18 material colours) 0.02% of pixels; t4b_matcher_real.out (k-means palettes) 0.7-14% mismatches with a mean extra dE of only 0.2-0.5.
kept.proposal: In nearestExact, brute-force CIEDE2000 over all allowed colours when the allowed count is 64 or less (sub-microsecond per colour). For larger palettes use K = 16 candidates. Keep the cache in nearest() but key it at 0.25 units, or document it as approximate. Add a unit test comparing nearestExact with brute force on random palettes of 8-200 colours.
corrected:
Leave the per-stone matching in mosaic.ts as it is (K=6 prefilter, cached). Brute force there doubles compute time for huge or dithered projects (8.3 s to 18.9 s at 667k cells) for an invisible gain (mean dE -0.001). Make only these small changes:

(1) In src/core/edits.ts removePaletteColor (lines 177-186), drop the NearestColorMatcher. Instead loop over the remaining palette colours and pick the minimum deltaE2000, or deltaE76 when formula is '76'. That is one query over at most 200 colours, so the cost is negligible, and the replacement is truly the nearest remaining colour.

(2) Rename NearestColorMatcher.nearestExact to nearestUncached and add a comment saying it is the CIE76 top-6 prefilter plus CIEDE2000 refinement, i.e. an approximation. Update the call in mosaic.ts:500.

(3) Optional: raise K from 6 to 12 only if a benchmark on a project of at least 600k cells with dithering shows no more than about 10% slowdown. On random palettes, K=16 cut misses from about 4.5% to about 0.6%.

(4) Add a vitest test: for 8-, 16- and 24-colour palettes, removePaletteColor's replacement must equal the brute-force CIEDE2000 nearest. Include the cited case: palette [#CAC2BB, #E3B684, #B5E74E, #5B9742, #C79F75, #0ED4AA, #1755F5, #90B4EC], query #043956, expected #1755F5.

1. Fix removing a colour exactly, at no speed cost (src/core/edits.ts:174-186). In removePaletteColor, drop the NearestColorMatcher. Loop over all remaining colours with deltaE(formula, palette[index].lab, palette[j].lab) (color.ts:175) and pick the smallest. This runs once per removal, so brute force costs nothing.

2. Make nearestExact exact for small palettes and much closer for large ones (src/core/color.ts:227-262):
   a. Count the allowed colours once in the constructor. If there are 16 or fewer, brute-force CIEDE2000 over all of them. Measured 2.6-3.9 µs for 8-12 colours versus 2.1 µs now. This covers own-material palettes and the 8/12/16-colour settings, where the large +10 to +30 dE errors occur.
   b. For more than 16 colours, keep a prefilter but rank by a symmetric CIE94-style distance instead of CIE76: dL² + dC²/(1+0.045·C̄)² + dH²/(1+0.015·C̄)², where dH² = max(0, da²+db²−dC²) and the chroma of each palette colour is computed once in the constructor. Keep the 10-12 best, then pick by CIEDE2000.
      - Measured with 200 random colours: wrong picks drop from 4.76% to 0.09%, worst extra from +6.3 to +0.54 dE.
      - k-means palettes: 0% wrong.
      - Cost: about 2x the current time per uncached query, not the 15x of brute force over 64.
   c. Leave the '76' formula path unchanged; it is already exact.
   d. Write the method's limits into its doc comment: exact for 16 or fewer colours; above that, worst measured extra about 0.5 dE. Alternatively rename it nearestFast so the name is honest.

3. Make the cache exact for whole and diagonal stones, again at no cost (color.ts:214-225). Do not shrink the key to 0.25 units. Instead build the L part of the key as Math.round(l*2.55), the same grid qL uses (mosaic.ts:87-89). Then rounded stone colours never share a cache entry. Today round(2L) puts some neighbouring L levels on the same key. Only cut pieces (SUB, which are not rounded) stay approximate, by under 0.5 dE; note that in a comment.

4. Tests (tests/core.test.ts), with a seeded generator:
   - nearestExact must equal brute-force CIEDE2000 on 100% of queries for random palettes of 8, 12 and 16 colours.
   - For 64 and 200 colours: fewer than 0.5% wrong and worst extra dE below 1.
   - A regression case built from the measured example: removing #E5D149 must pick #FFF4C2 over #7DAE48.
   - Check that colour counts still add up to the stone total after removePaletteColor.

5. Benchmark guard: time a dithered run of about 1M stones with 200 colours before and after. Accept at most about 2x slower assignment. If it is slower than that, use K=8, which measured 0.22% wrong and worst +2.0 dE at about 1.8x the time.

kept.title: parseCellId accepts invalid piece suffixes ('A001-0' gives piece -1), so stone search silently fails
kept.problem: The regex accepts any digits after '-'. 'A001-0' yields piece -1 and 'A001-99' yields piece 98 without checking against the cell's piece count. In StepPreview the search then opens nothing for -1 (StoneDialog gets pieces[-1] = undefined and returns null), or opens a different piece than typed, with no message.
kept.evidence: src/core/layout.ts:189-196; src/ui/project/StepPreview.tsx:66-70; src/ui/project/StoneDialog.tsx:57-58,79. /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-core/t1_layout.out: 'parseCellId "A001-0" {"row":0,"col":0,"piece":-1}', 'parseCellId "A001-99" {"row":0,"col":0,"piece":98}'.
kept.proposal: Change the regex to `-([1-9]\d*)` so the piece is at least 1. In StepPreview, check piece < cellPieceCount(data, idx) and show a 'Stein nicht gefunden' message otherwise. Add these cases to the layout tests.
corrected:
1) In src/core/layout.ts:190, change the suffix group to `-([1-9]\d*)` so that "-0" and "-00" no longer parse. Keep parseCellId free of any piece-count check, because it only receives the layout and not the data.

2) In src/ui/project/StepPreview.tsx, inside the onSubmit at lines 63-72:
- Call parseCellId.
- If the result is null, or `p.piece >= cellPieceCount(c.data, p.row*c.layout.cols + p.col)` (import it from core/pieces), set a local `searchMsg` state to `t('preview.stoneNotFound')`. Render it under the input in `<small className="muted" role="status">`.
- Otherwise clear the message, call setPick and center.
- One exception: when the cell has only one piece and the user typed "-1", accept it as piece 0, which the current code already does.

3) Add 'preview.stoneNotFound' to src/i18n/de.ts, en.ts and tr.ts:
- de: 'Stein nicht gefunden'
- en: 'Stone not found'
- tr: 'Taş bulunamadı'

4) Optionally, make render.ts:282 and StoneDialog.tsx:57 agree: either both use the validated piece, or both clamp the same way. With the validation from step 2 they can no longer disagree.

5) Add unit cases to tests/core.test.ts: parseCellId(L,'A001-0')===null, 'A001-00'===null, and 'A001-2' gives piece 1.

Priority: low (impact 1, effort S). Bundle it with other polish in StepPreview rather than doing it as a separate item.

1) src/core/layout.ts parseCellId: change the regex to /^([A-Za-z]+)(\d+)(?:-([1-9]\d*))?$/ so piece is always >= 0. Optionally make it take an optional pieceCount argument and return null when piece >= pieceCount, to keep validation in the core.

2) src/ui/project/StepPreview.tsx onSubmit:
- Compute p = parseCellId(c.layout, search).
- If p is non-null, set idx = p.row*c.layout.cols + p.col and n = cellPieceCount(c.data, idx) (import from core/pieces, as StepPlan.tsx:100 already does).
- If p is null, or p.piece >= n (with one tolerance: accept '-1' on a 1-piece cell as piece 0), set a local findMsg state and do not change pick. Clear findMsg on success and on input change.
- Render findMsg under the form as <small className="error" role="status">.

3) Add i18n keys 'preview.notFound' to src/i18n/de.ts, en.ts and tr.ts. Example DE text: 'Stein „{id}“ nicht gefunden – gültige Positionen: A001 bis {last}'. Compute {last} with cellId(c.layout, c.layout.rows-1, c.layout.cols-1), so the message only states real, computed bounds. For a valid cell with a bad piece suffix, add 'preview.pieceNotFound': '{cell} hat nur {n} Teilstück(e)'.

4) Make the dialog and highlight agree (defensive): in src/core/render.ts:283, change the fallback from `ps[piece] ?? ps[0]` to the same clamp StoneDialog uses (ps[Math.max(0, Math.min(piece, ps.length-1))]). Also clamp to >= 0 in StoneDialog.tsx:57 (`Math.max(0, Math.min(p.piece, pieces.length-1))`), so neither can ever point at different stones.

5) tests/core.test.ts: add cases to the 'Zeilenbezeichnungen' test:
- parseCellId(L,'A001-0') === null
- parseCellId(L,'A001-00') === null
- parseCellId(L,'A001-2').piece === 1
- an out-of-grid ID returns null
- a lowercase/whitespace ID still parses

Optionally extend e2e/run-e2e.cjs: type 'ZZ9999' into data-testid=find-stone and assert the not-found message is visible.

kept.title: Leaving a project while it is still computing, then reopening it, corrupts the saved project: the mosaic is rendered and printed with the wrong palette
kept.problem: compute() runs in a module-level worker channel and keeps running after the Workspace unmounts. When it finishes, it saves its own record and mosaic. If the user reopens the project in the meantime, the new useProject instance loads the OLD record and mosaic. It shows no 'computing' indicator. Its next save of the record (any rename or setting change) overwrites the record written by compute but leaves compute's new mosaic in place. Record and mosaic are saved by unrelated, non-atomic puts. Nothing ties them together (no revision), so the loader accepts any pair that has the same cols×rows. As a result, colour indices from one compute are mapped onto the palette of another. The same race applies to two open browser tabs.
kept.evidence: Repro: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-ui-state/t10_leave_during_compute.cjs, output in t10_output.txt in the same folder. City sample, 260,241 positions. Compute with 16 colours, then switch to 8 colours and recompute. Leave via 'Meine Projekte', reopen ('palette rows = 16, computing indicator visible: false'), rename, reload. Result: 'palette rows = 16', and the legend shows 01..08 used and 09..16 with 0 stones. The city is rendered in pink/yellow; screenshot t10-after-reload.png in the same folder. Code: useProject.ts:331-346 (compute saves rec, mosaic and progress with Promise.all as 3 separate transactions, from the snapshot r); useProject.ts:86-94 (loader only checks layout.cols/rows); client.ts:5-12 (one global 'compute' worker, with no per-project job state); db.ts:96-102 (independent puts).
kept.proposal: (1) Track jobs per project in a small module-level registry, e.g. src/workers/jobs.ts with Map<projectId, {promise, progress}>. useProject subscribes on mount, so a reopened Workspace shows the running compute and its Cancel button and refreshes when the job finishes. (2) Add db.saveComputed(id, rec, mosaic, progress), which writes all three stores in ONE IndexedDB transaction (db.transaction(['projects','mosaics','progress'],'readwrite')). (3) Add a revision: rec.mosaicRev = uid() is written together with mosaic.rev. The loader shows the mosaic only if rec.mosaicRev === mosaic.rev && max colour index < palette.length. Otherwise it shows 'Gespeichertes Mosaik passt nicht zur Palette – bitte neu berechnen' instead of rendering wrong colours. (4) Optimistic concurrency in saveProject: inside one readwrite transaction, read the stored meta.rev, refuse to overwrite a newer revision, and tell the user (this also covers two tabs).
corrected:
(1) Move compute ownership out of the component. Create src/workers/jobs.ts with Map<projectId, {promise, progress, cancel}>.
- The job itself does the final persist, so it no longer depends on setRec/setComputed of a possibly unmounted hook.
- useProject subscribes on mount. A reopened Workspace then shows the running progress and the Cancel button, and adopts the result (setRec + setComputed) when the job resolves.

(2) Add saveComputed(id, computedFields, mosaic, progress) in src/storage/db.ts. It runs ONE readwrite transaction over ['projects','mosaics','progress']:
- Read the CURRENT stored record.
- Merge in only the compute-owned fields: palette, diagnostics, computedWith, meta.computed, meta.thumb, and a new mosaicRev = uid().
- Put the record, the mosaic {...mosaic, rev: mosaicRev} and the progress in that same transaction.
This way a rename or other edit made during the compute is not lost, and record and mosaic can never be half-written.

(3) Make the loader in useProject.ts:85-98 validate the pair. Accept the stored mosaic only if rec.mosaicRev === mosaic.rev AND every colour index (c1, c2, subCol, free[].color) is less than palette.length. Otherwise do not render it. Show a clear notice such as 'Gespeichertes Mosaik passt nicht zur Palette – bitte neu berechnen' and keep the Preview, Plan and PDF steps disabled until the user recomputes.
- The palette-length check alone is not enough. In the photo-replace and two-tab repros the indices are within range and the stale badge is not shown.
- Treat legacy records without a rev the same way: run the index-range check and show a soft warning.

(4) For saves from other instances (useProject.update and flush, and the two-tab case), change saveProject to run as one readwrite transaction:
- Read the stored record.
- If stored.mosaicRev differs from the in-memory rec.mosaicRev, keep the stored compute-owned fields (palette, computedWith, diagnostics, mosaicRev, thumb) and apply only the user's edits on top. Do not silently refuse the save.
- Post a BroadcastChannel('mosaicplan') message {id, mosaicRev} from saveComputed. Open tabs or instances of the same project then reload the record and mosaic, or show 'In einem anderen Tab neu berechnet – neu laden'.
- Palette edits made after the compute (custom names, material assignment) must update mosaicRev only when the mapping from colour index to colour changes. Edits that only change names keep the rev.

(5) Add an e2e test based on verify-correctness-ui-state-0/v1_leave_during_compute.cjs and v3_two_tabs.cjs. It must assert that after the reload the stored palette, the computedWith key and the mosaic all come from the same compute.

Fix in four parts, in this order of priority.

1) Commit compute results atomically and safely (src/storage/db.ts).
- Add commitComputed(id, patch, mosaic, progress, rev). It opens ONE transaction: db.transaction(['projects','mosaics','progress'], 'readwrite').
- Inside onsuccess callbacks only (no await on non-IDB promises), it does: get('projects', id).
  - If the record is missing (project was deleted), abort and reject with 'deleted'.
  - Otherwise put {...latest, palette, diagnostics, computedWith, mosaicRev: rev, meta: {...latest.meta, computed: true, thumb, updatedAt}}.
  - Then put mosaics[id] = {...packed, rev} and progress[id].
- Prepare thumb, packMosaic and computeKey BEFORE opening the transaction.
- computedWith = computeKey of the snapshot settings that were computed (in custom mode, together with the result palette), never of the merged record. This way, edits made during the compute correctly show as 'stale' and are not lost (this also fixes t2: rename and joint change during a compute).
- Also add a multi-store tx helper. deleteProject should use one transaction over all four stores.

2) Per-project job registry (new src/workers/jobs.ts).
- Holds Map<projectId, {progress, promise, cancel}> plus a subscribe(id, cb) API.
- Move the worker call and commitComputed out of the component closure into startCompute(id, input).
- Allow only one compute at a time across the app. If a job for another project is running, the compute button shows 'Berechnung für „<Name>“ läuft noch' with Abbrechen.
- useProject subscribes on mount:
  - It shows the running job's phase/fraction and the Cancel button.
  - On commit it does setRec(prev => ({...prev, palette, diagnostics, computedWith, mosaicRev, meta: {...prev.meta, computed: true, thumb}})).
  - It replaces computedRef/state with the committed grid.
  - It clears pending 'mosaic'/'progress' save timers that refer to the old grid.
- While a job is running for the project, disable stone edits on the old grid in a reopened instance.
- Projects.tsx: deleting a project with a running job cancels that job first.

3) Integrity guard in the loader (useProject.ts:85-98).
- Render the stored grid only if both conditions hold:
  - (rec.mosaicRev === undefined && mosaic.rev === undefined) [legacy data], OR rec.mosaicRev === mosaic.rev;
  - AND max colour index < rec.palette.length (a single pass over the Uint16 colour array).
- Otherwise, set computed = null. Show a banner (de/en/tr): 'Gespeichertes Mosaik passt nicht zur Palette – bitte neu berechnen', with the Berechnen button. Never render, plan or print the mismatched pair.
- Every writer that changes what colour indices mean must write both revs in one transaction: compute, palette compaction/removal, and import. Manual stone edits that only append palette entries keep the existing rev, so they cannot trigger false positives.
- Include rev in export/duplicate. Imports without a rev take the legacy path.
- Also block the PDF and plan steps when stale is true, or at least show a prominent warning on the PDF cover/first page.

4) Instead of optimistic concurrency in saveProject, guard against two tabs with the Web Locks API.
- Workspace calls navigator.locks.request('project:' + id, {ifAvailable: true}, lock => lock ? new Promise(release on unmount) : null).
- If the lock is not granted, open the project read-only with the banner 'Dieses Projekt ist in einem anderen Tab geöffnet'.
- This avoids the false-conflict and silent-save-refusal risk of rev checks on every debounced save.

Tests:
- Extend e2e/run-e2e.cjs with these flows:
  - Leave during compute, reopen, check that progress and Cancel are visible, then rename, reload, and check palette length == max index + 1 and colours as computed.
  - The same, but set the colour count back, and check that no wrong grid is shown as 'berechnet'.
  - Delete during compute, then check that the project does not come back.
- Add a vitest unit test: the loader guard rejects a mismatched rev or an out-of-range index.

kept.title: Edits from the last 0.4–1.2 s are lost on reload or tab close because the 'pagehide' save never completes
kept.problem: Saves are debounced: the record after 400 ms, progress after 600 ms, the mosaic after 1200 ms. The only safety net is flush() on 'pagehide'/'visibilitychange'. flush() goes through open().then(...) and starts asynchronous IndexedDB transactions that the browser tears down before they commit. So stone colour or shape changes, lay-mode taps and renames made shortly before a reload or tab close are lost silently. On Android, switching apps fires 'visibilitychange' first, which mitigates this. On PC and tablet browsers (refresh, closing the tab, browser restart) the data is lost.
kept.evidence: Repro: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-ui-state/t4_reload_mid_edit.cjs. With a 50 ms delay (t4_output_50ms.txt): '(a) J020 colour 09 -> 13 ... after reload = 09 -> LOST', '(b) placed in UI = 5 ... after reload placed = 0', '(c) name ... = Test: Tier (Katze)'. At 500 ms the stone edit is still lost. At 1600 ms everything persists (t4_output_1600ms.txt). Trace t4b_pagehide_trace.cjs / t4b_output.txt: '[trace] pagehide at 3186', '[trace] put projects at 3187', then neither 'complete' nor 'abort' is logged. The write is issued but never committed. Code: useProject.ts:107-113 (schedule), 133-142 (pagehide flush), 151/166/179 (400/1200/600 ms).
kept.proposal: (1) Write progress and single-stone edits through almost immediately: coalesce with queueMicrotask or setTimeout(…,50) instead of 600/1200 ms. Saving progress is one Uint16Array put. For very large mosaics, store dirty cell indices in a small 'patches' store and compact later. (2) Keep the resolved IDBDatabase in a plain variable, so flush() can create its transaction synchronously inside the event handler. (3) On the web build, add a 'beforeunload' handler that calls e.preventDefault() while saveTimers is non-empty or a save is in flight, so the browser shows 'Seite verlassen?'. (4) Show a small 'Gespeichert ✓ / Speichert…' indicator in the Workspace header, driven by the same pending-save counter.
corrected:
1. In src/storage/db.ts tx(): after `const r = fn(s);`, add `if (mode === 'readwrite' && typeof (t as any).commit === 'function') (t as any).commit();`. Every write here issues exactly one request, so this is safe. It tells the browser to commit right away instead of waiting for the success callback, which never comes while the page is unloading.

2. In src/ui/project/useProject.ts, in the effect at lines 133-142, also register `window.addEventListener('beforeunload', h)` and remove it in the cleanup. 'beforeunload' fires before the old document is torn down, and together with commit() the write survives a reload (measured 5 of 5; the full app simulation persisted all edits).
   - Keep the existing 'pagehide' and 'visibilitychange' handlers, which cover Android app switching.
   - Do not save the whole mosaic every 50 ms.
   - Optionally lower the progress debounce from 600 ms to about 250 ms, since saving progress is a single Uint16Array put.

3. kept.title: Full-resolution photos are kept decoded and never released (ImageBitmap.close() is never called), and PDF object URLs leak
kept.problem: Each Workspace mount decodes the original photo at full resolution (a 48 MP phone photo is about 190 MB of RGBA). Home.newProject decodes it once more only to read the aspect ratio. Nothing calls bitmap.close(): not on photo replacement, not on unmount, not in Home. Memory stays high after leaving the project, which risks renderer or WebView crashes on Android phones (which in turn hit the unsaved-debounce problem). StepPdf also creates an object URL for every generated PDF and never revokes it, so each regeneration keeps the previous multi-MB blob alive.
kept.evidence: Measurement: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/correctness-ui-state/t13_bitmap_memory.cjs with big48mp.jpg (8000×6000), output t13_output.txt: Chromium RSS 'baseline 450' → 'after opening 779' → 880–1127 MB while reopening 6 times → 'after leaving project, 5 s idle 1108' MB (not released). Code: grep finds no '.close()' in src; imagePrep.ts:10-16 (full-res createImageBitmap), Home.tsx:29 and 44, useProject.ts:79/188-192, StepPdf.tsx:71 (createObjectURL with no revoke; downloadBlob in components.tsx:162-169 does revoke).
kept.proposal: On import, downscale to a working copy (long edge ≤ 4096 px, enough for 40M positions) using createImageBitmap(blob, {resizeWidth, resizeQuality:'high'}). Store it as the 'working' image and keep the original blob only for export. Call bmp.close() in Home after reading width/height, in setPhoto before replacing, and in a useProject unmount cleanup. In StepPdf, revoke the previous result.url before setResult and in a useEffect cleanup.
corrected:
Low priority (impact about 2, effort S). Change only where memory is freed; image quality stays the same.

1. Keep two images in useProject.ts:
   - A preview bitmap for the screens, decoded with createImageBitmap(blob, {imageOrientation:'from-image', resizeWidth/resizeHeight so the long edge is at most 4096, resizeQuality:'high'}). StepPhoto, CropEditor, StepShapes, StepGeometry and originalPreview use it, and crop coordinates stay normalized.
   - The real photo size, kept in state as `sourceSize`. Use it for the "W x H px" label in StepPhoto.tsx:104 and for the aspect-ratio math.
2. Decode the full-resolution photo only during compute. In runCompute (useProject.ts:277-290), decode image.original, pass it to renderCropped, then call close() in a finally block right after canvasToRaw. Compute input is then exactly what it is today.
3. Call close() on the old bitmap in three places: in setPhoto before setBitmap, in a useEffect cleanup keyed on the bitmap, and in the load effect when `alive` is false.
4. In Home.tsx:29 and 44, call close() right after reading width and height.
5. In StepPdf, keep the URL in a ref. Revoke the previous URL before setResult({url}), and revoke the current one in an unmount cleanup.

Check the result with mem3.cjs: at most one bitmap alive at any time, and renderer memory down when a project is reopened.

Part A (effort S, do it now; compute results stay identical):
1. **Home.tsx:29-30 and 44-45:** close the bitmap right after reading the aspect:
   `const b = await loadBitmap(photo); aspect = b.width / b.height; b.close();`
2. **useProject.ts:79-80:** `if (alive) setBitmap(bmp); else bmp.close();`
3. **useProject.ts:** release the old bitmap only after React has committed the new one, never inside `setPhoto` before `setBitmap`:
   ```
   const liveBmp = useRef<ImageBitmap|null>(null);
   useEffect(() => { const old = liveBmp.current; liveBmp.current = bitmap; if (old && old !== bitmap) old.close(); }, [bitmap]);
   useEffect(() => () => { liveBmp.current?.close(); liveBmp.current = null; }, []);
   ```
   This is safe under StrictMode because the bitmap is still null when StrictMode does its test unmount.
4. **StepPdf `generate`:** call `api.originalPreview(1800)` and encode it before the first await, or wrap it in try/catch. Then leaving mid-generation can never draw a closed bitmap.
5. **StepPdf object URL:**
   - Create it only when `!isNative()`.
   - Keep it in `urlRef`, and revoke the previous one when a new generation starts.
   - Add `useEffect(() => () => { if (urlRef.current) URL.revokeObjectURL(urlRef.current); }, [])` above the early `if (!c || !G) return`.
6. **Regression check:** add a Playwright case that opens a project with a large photo, goes to Projects, reopens it, and checks that the photo step still shows the real pixel size and that Compute and PDF work.

Part B (effort M, optional; keep two versions of the image instead of shrinking the one used for the calculation):
1. On load, decode a preview bitmap with `createImageBitmap(blob, {imageOrientation:'from-image', resizeWidth, resizeHeight, resizeQuality:'high'})`, long edge at most 3072-4096.
2. Use it for StepPhoto, CropEditor, StepShapes and originalPreview, and for `effectiveCrop`. The crop is stored as fractions of the image, so it is the same at any size.
3. Store the original width and height when the photo is imported, and show those as the "px" size.
4. In `compute()`, decode the full-resolution original from `api.image.original` on demand, then run `renderCropped` and `canvasToRaw`, then close it right away. The working image stays exactly as today (up to 6 MP of the crop), so tight crops such as faces keep full colour detail.
5. Do not feed a 4096 copy into `workingSize` as the compute source.

kept.title: Opening a computed project from 'Meine Projekte' lands on step 1 'Foto' instead of Preview or Plan
kept.problem: The intended auto-jump (Workspace.tsx:28-31: if computed and no initialStep, go to 'preview') never fires when the project is opened from the list or Home. go('#/project/id') sets location.hash, the Workspace mount effect immediately calls history.replaceState('#/project/id/photo'), and then the queued hashchange event reads the replaced hash. useHash then hands Workspace initialStep='photo'. So a user who comes back to a project to keep laying stones always starts at the photo upload and crop screen.

Code: App.tsx:18-23 (go sets the hash and the state), App.tsx:14 (hashchange → setHash(location.hash)), Workspace.tsx:23-31.
kept.proposal: In Workspace, capture the route step once on mount (const initial = useRef(initialStep)) and use it for both the useState initialiser and the auto-jump effect. Or have useHash ignore a hashchange whose path only adds a step suffix to the current project route. When a project has progress > 0, open the 'plan' step instead of 'preview' (resume laying).
corrected:
In src/ui/project/Workspace.tsx, capture the route step once on mount with `const initialRef = useRef(initialStep);`. Keep the existing useState initialiser, which already runs only once. In the auto-jump effect, test `initialRef.current` instead of the `initialStep` prop:

`useEffect(() => { if (api.loaded && api.computed && !initialRef.current) setStep(api.progress && api.progress.total.placed > 0 ? 'plan' : 'preview'); }, [api.loaded]);`

`api.progress` comes from useProject.ts:222-228 and has the shape `{ total: { placed, total }, perSection }`. The late hashchange will still pass initialStep='photo', but it no longer affects anything, because Workspace is keyed by id and ignores later prop changes.

Don't change useHash or go(). A real deep link with a step (e.g. #/project/<id>/plan) keeps working, because initialRef then holds that step.

Optional cleanup in the same area: Home.tsx:34 has a no-op ternary `photo ? 'photo' : 'photo'`.

Add an e2e assertion to e2e/run-e2e.cjs. After compute, go to 'Meine Projekte', click the project row link, and expect `.step.active` to contain 'Vorschau'. If any stones are marked laid, expect 'Verlegeplan' instead.

For a single-section project, or when the limit is reached at a cell boundary in the last section, the PDF ends without the 'gekürzt' notice. The list looks complete but is not.
kept.evidence: Repro /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/pdf-print/trunc.ts prints "cells=256 coordLimit=100 coordRowsPrinted=100 truncationNoticePresent=false" (and the same for 200).
