Put a status in each section's table title, e.g. 'Koordinaten A1 (1.734 von 1.852 Steinen – Rest siehe CSV)'. Add a vitest case: single section with coordLimit < pieces must contain the notice.
corrected:
In src/core/pdf.ts (coordinate block, about lines 814-864), decide truncation from the loop itself instead of comparing against a separately computed total:
1. Remove `&& written < opts.coordLimit` from the row and column loop conditions. Use a labelled outer loop (`outer: for (let row ...)`).
2. Inside the column loop, call `const ps = cellPieces(...)`. Then: `if (ps.length && written >= opts.coordLimit) { truncated = true; secTruncated = true; break outer; }`. Keep the existing forEach guard for a cell cut in the middle. That guard should also set secTruncated.
3. Keep the existing check between sections (818-820).
4. If secTruncated, add the status to the section's table title, for example `Koordinaten – Abschnitt A1 (erste 1.734 Steine – gekürzt, vollständige Liste als CSV)`. Count the number shown with the same cellPieces-based count the loop uses. Also print the existing pdf.coordsTruncated text right under the last table. Keep the separate notice page as well, or replace it with this.
5. Add a vitest case in tests/pdf.test.ts: a single section with squares only and coordLimit smaller than the pieces must contain the notice. A second case selects only the last section via sectionIds with a small coordLimit. A third case with coordLimit at or above the pieces must not contain the notice.

kept.title: Cut-template dimension labels print over the title and the info text, so dimensions are hard to read
kept.problem: Edge-length labels are pushed outward by 0.9 raw-mm, and that offset is multiplied by the zoom (pdf.ts:781; zoom is 6 for 5 mm stones, so 5.4 mm on paper). Top-edge labels land in the title row. Bottom-edge labels land on the first info line, which starts at a fixed oy+rawH*zoom+3.5 (pdf.ts:783). Info lines wrap through maxWidth but only advance 2.8 mm per logical line (pdf.ts:795-799), so the 'Farben' list prints over the ID list. kept.problem: renderMosaic is immediate-mode. For each visible cell it sets fillStyle and calls fillRect. Viewer.draw runs this on every pointermove and wheel event (Viewer.tsx:55 to 78, 196 to 207). It also calls getComputedStyle on every frame (Viewer.tsx:75). Nothing is cached between frames, so the cost is set by the number of visible cells. That number is highest just above the overview threshold (pitch 3 px or more and cellCount ≤ 400k, render.ts:165).
kept.evidence: Tablet emulation (1280x800 at DPR 2, CDP CPU throttling 4x), 200x100 cm at 5 mm (55,778 positions), preview step, 20 pan moves per zoom level (browser-big.cjs with TABLET=1 THROTTLE=4, browser/t55k/result.json). rAF callback time: zoom step 4 median 80.9 ms, p95 122 ms; step 6 91.8 / 156 ms; step 16 99.7 / 164 ms; step 18 101 / 254 ms. 20 of 20 frames were long tasks at these levels. Desktop without throttling: 55k step 2 median 16 ms, p95 33.5 ms; 5M step 14 median 23.2 ms, p95 36.9 ms (browser/b55k, browser/b5m). CPU profile while panning (browser-prof-pan.cjs, browser/profpan/pan-4 and pan-16.cpuprofile): at the face-overview zoom fillRect is 20.6 % of all samples; at the nose zoom drawImage (glaze) is 16.1 % and fillRect 10.7 %. kept.proposal: Add a tile cache. Quantize the zoom into power-of-two buckets, render 256x256 device-pixel tiles into OffscreenCanvas or ImageBitmap, ideally in a render worker using canvas.transferControlToOffscreen. Keep an LRU of about 64 tiles. Each frame then only draws the roughly 20 to 40 tiles that intersect the view, scaled between buckets, and switches to exact tiles once interaction settles. An edit or progress change invalidates only the tile containing that cell. Draw the selection, sections and progress ticks as a light overlay layer. For pitch 3 to 8 px, fill tiles through ImageData (cell color into a Uint32Array) instead of one fillRect per cell. Apply the glaze once per tile with createPattern aligned to the grid, instead of one drawImage per stone. Read --viewer-bg once, not every frame.
corrected:
Phase 1 (M effort, recommended):

1. Add a back buffer in Viewer.tsx. Use an OffscreenCanvas, or a hidden canvas, sized to the viewport plus a margin of about 25 % on each side, in device pixels. Render it with the existing renderMosaic at the current scale, without the highlight and section overlays. Store the view (scale, ox, oy) it was rendered for.

2. Pan: each frame, copy the buffer onto the visible canvas with one drawImage at the pan offset. When the view nears the edge of the margin, shift the buffer contents with drawImage onto itself. Then call renderMosaic only for the newly exposed strips. Use a View whose width and height cover just the strip, translated with ctx.translate and clipped to the strip rect. visibleRange then limits the work to those cells.

3. Wheel and pinch zoom: while the gesture runs, draw the buffer scaled. About 120-150 ms after the last wheel or pinch event, render the buffer again at the exact scale.

4. Invalidation: the cache key is all the props in the existing draw-effect dependency list (Viewer.tsx:142-144): layout, version, palette, realistic, showCodes, progressMode, focusColor, groutHex, surface, plus DPR.
   - Any change to these re-renders the whole buffer once.
   - For a single-stone colour edit or a progress tap, re-render only that cell's rect, with clip and the restricted view. This needs the Viewer to receive the changed row and col from useProject.

5. Overlays: draw the highlight and the section borders and labels after the blit, every frame. They are a few dozen calls. Selecting a stone or a section then never invalidates the buffer.

6. Read --viewer-bg once, on mount and when the theme or data-theme changes, not in every frame.

7. Keep the glaze per cell inside the cached render. Do NOT replace it with one createPattern: edge columns and rows have different sizes (layout.ts:71-104), and cut or freeform pieces are polygons.

8. Add an e2e guard for requirement 18:
   - After a pan and a single-stone edit, compare getImageData of the cached viewer with a fresh uncached renderMosaic of the same view. The difference must be within an anti-aliasing tolerance.
   - Re-run pan-verify.cjs. Target: the rAF callback stays under 4 ms during pan at 4x throttle on the tablet profile.

Phase 2 (optional, L effort, only if Phase 1 is not enough on real Android devices):
- Use 256x256 device-pixel tiles in power-of-two scale buckets, with an LRU of about 64 tiles.
- Consider a render worker only if the mosaic data can be shared read-only and stays in sync with edits and progress.

Effort M, impact 3 (4 on tablets and phones). Keep src/core/render.ts output unchanged, because renderFull feeds the PDF preview and thumbnails. Implement the caching only in src/ui/project/Viewer.tsx.

1) Split rendering into a cached base layer and a cheap overlay.

   - Read --viewer-bg once (on mount and on theme or matchMedia change), not per frame.

   - When the viewport leaves the cached margin, re-render the base around the new centre. This happens once every several hundred px of drag, not every frame. Optionally render only the newly exposed strips by clipping renderMosaic to them.

3) Wheel and pinch zoom.
   - For in-between frames, draw the cached base with a scale transform (temporarily blurry is acceptable).

   - Never leave a scaled frame as the final, settled image.

4) Invalidation (the correctness-critical part).
   - Any change of a key field throws away the whole base.

At large grids the working image has only about 0.1 to 3 source pixels per cell (workingSize is capped at 6 MP or at the photo size), so sub-cell edges cannot be resolved, yet the full search still runs. The only safeguard is a grey sentence below the button. The 'stale' badge also keeps prompting the user to recompute after any setting change.

1) Guard (effort S, highest value). In StepCompute's onClick, compute `placed = api.progress?.total.placed` and a `hasEdits` flag (see step 3). If either is non-zero, show a modal instead of a passive line. Example text: "1.526 verlegte Steine und manuelle Änderungen gehen verloren." The backup button calls the existing duplicateProject(id, t('compute.backupSuffix')) from src/storage/projects.ts, which already copies the record, image, mosaic and progress, then calls api.compute(). 2) Exact progress carry-over (effort M), only when it can be proven exact. Inside compute(), before replacing computedRef, keep `old = computedRef.current`. kept.title: Mixed tile sizes (req. 3) exist only as k×k cuts of the base stone, in sizes the user cannot choose, and are almost never used
kept.problem: Requirement 3 asks for different tile sizes in one project, with real positions and dimensions for each stone. The only mechanism is splitting a base cell into k×k pieces. The fine size is forced by (w−(k−1)g)/k, which is often not a size you can buy. Every fine piece is counted as cut from the large raw tile, because there is only one raw size per colour. The user therefore cannot plan 'fine stones from my 4 mm tiles'. The optimiser also almost never picks subdivision, even inside a marked face, so requirement 5 ('finer stones in faces, eyes, hair') is effectively not met.

LINE wins because its penalty is 1.4·λ, against 2·λ for subdivision (mosaic.ts:336, :364). The raw size is set per colour only (src/core/stats.ts:73-81). kept.proposal: Add 'Zonen mit eigenem Raster'. Zone {id, c0,c1,r0,r1 (base-grid index range), tileW, tileH, joint}. Zone span Lx = colX[c1−1]+colW[c1−1]−colX[c0], which is exact because it ends at stone outer edges. Inner grid = computeLayout({widthMm:Lx, heightMm:Ly, tileW, tileH, joint, edgeMode:'cut-both'}), offset by (colX[c0], rowY[r0]). The zone border lies in the base joint, so the gap between zone and base stones is exactly the base joint g. Base cells inside the zone get a new CellKind.ZONE with 0 pieces, so nothing is counted twice. The zone gets its own MosaicData from computeMosaic on the zone sub-image, with fixedPalette set to the project palette. If computeAxis returns rest>0, show the remainder rather than silently stretching. Offer exact-fit snapping. Example: base 10/2 mm with a 4/2 mm zone always fits, since 12n−2 = 2n·4+(2n−1)·2. Base 8/1 mm with a 4/1 mm zone fits whenever n is a multiple of 5. IDs 'Z1:A001' with absolute X/Y. Stats, CSV and PDF iterate the base grid plus zones. Raw material is chosen per (colour, tile size), so zone stones are uncut real tiles. splitAxis must not place section boundaries inside a zone span. The step-6 region tool creates zones from face or detail rectangles. Quick win first (S): replace the k choice with a 'target fine size' and offer only k where (w+g) = k·(w2+g). kept.title: No undo/redo and no area or batch editing: every correction is one irreversible single-stone click
kept.problem: Requirement 13 (manually change stones, e.g. 'lighter blue') can only be done one piece at a time, and nothing can be undone. Removing a palette colour remaps every stone permanently. A shape change clears that cell's laying progress. A core function to replace a colour within a range already exists but is not reachable from the UI. Correcting a sky or a background means hundreds of separate clicks with no safety net.
kept.evidence: Reproduction /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/spec-gaps/b1.cjs. Grep finds no undo in src except 'free.undoPoint' (the freeform point editor). replaceColor in src/core/edits.ts:209 has no caller in src/ui. removePaletteColor is called from src/ui/project/StepColors.tsx:112. setCellKind sets progress to 0 (src/core/edits.ts:77). Each operation stores CellSnapshot{idx, kind, c1, c2, sub?, line?, free?, progress} before and after; only the few affected Map entries are cloned. Palette operations store the previous palette plus the (idx, piece, oldColor) tuples they changed. Cap the stack at about 200 operations or 32 MB. Add ↶/↷ buttons in Preview and Plan, Ctrl/Cmd+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z, and 'letzten Tap zurück' in laying mode. Add a selection tool in Viewer: a rectangle or lasso in mm, selecting by piece-centroid test. Actions on the selection or section: 'Farbe A → B' (reuse replaceColor with Range); 'heller/dunkler', which picks the palette colour with the smallest ΔE among those with L* ≥ current+3 or ≤ current−3; and 'Form zurücksetzen'. corrected:
Deliver this in three phases. Phase A is cheapest and helps most.

**Phase A (S): batch colour replacement and two data-loss fixes.**
- **Section panel** (StepPlan.tsx, next to the existing mark/reset buttons, around lines 205-225): add "Farbe A → B in diesem Abschnitt". Section already has r0/r1/c0/c1, so pass it straight to replaceColor(c.layout, c.data, from, to, sec), then call api.touchMosaic() and show the returned count.
- **Palette table** (StepColors.tsx): add "alle Steine dieser Farbe → Farbe X" for the whole mosaic, without deleting the colour (replaceColor with no range).
- **Confirm before deleting a colour** (StepColors.tsx remove()): show a confirm() that names the stone count and the target colour code.
- **Stop needless progress resets** (edits.ts setCellKind): return early without touching anything when the kind is unchanged (for LINE, also with the same parameters; for SUB, also with the same k). Also keep progress for a FULL ↔ DIAG change only if a future decision allows it. The minimum fix is: do not clear progress on a no-op.

**Phase B (M): undo and redo.**
- **Journal module.** Add src/core/editJournal.ts, kept in memory and cleared whenever computeMosaic produces new data.
- **Cell operations.** For setPieceColor, setCellKind, setFreePieces, togglePiecePlaced, setCellPlaced, setRangePlaced and replaceColor, store per-cell before/after snapshots: {idx, kind, c1, c2, progress, sub?, line?, free?}, with the Map entries cloned. A batch operation becomes one entry holding many snapshots.
- **Palette operations.** For removePaletteColor (and updatePaletteColor), store the previous palette array. For removal, also store only the pieces that had the removed colour, as (idx, piece). Undo works in two steps: first map every colour value v ≥ removedIndex back to v + 1 across c1, c2, sub and free (the inverse of remapAll), then restore the recorded pieces to removedIndex. As a simpler alternative, snapshot packMosaic(data) for palette operations only; that is about 8 MB at 2 M cells.
- **Limits.** Cap the journal at about 200 entries or about 32 MB and drop the oldest first.
- **UI.** Add ↶/↷ buttons in StepPreview and StepPlan. Bind Ctrl/Cmd+Z and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z only when focus is not in an input field. After every undo or redo, call touchMosaic or touchProgress so stats are recomputed through the existing worker effect (useProject.ts:239ff) and the change is saved.

**Phase C (M): rectangle selection in Viewer.**
- **Selection mode.** A toggle that turns drag-to-pan into drag-to-select. Convert the mm rectangle into a row/col Range using layout.colX and layout.rowY, so stats.Range is reused.
- **Actions.** "Farbe A → B" (replaceColor with that range), "Form zurücksetzen" (setCellKind FULL for each cell), and "heller/dunkler". For each piece, "heller/dunkler" picks the existing palette colour with the smallest ΔE2000 among those with L* ≥ L*cur + 3 (or ≤ L*cur − 3). Pieces with no such colour stay unchanged and are counted in the result message. No new colours are ever invented.
- **Undo.** Each action is one journal entry.
- **Lasso.** Defer it. If it is added later, select pieces by a centroid-in-polygon test.

**Tests.** In tests/, check that undo after each operation restores packMosaic output byte for byte, and that progress totals are unchanged after undo.

Phase 0 (S, ship first): guard the destructive actions.
- StepColors.tsx:108 remove(): count how many stones use the colour (api.stats.perColor[i].pieces) and find the target through the same NearestColorMatcher as removePaletteColor. Then call confirm(t('colors.removeConfirm', {n, code, name, targetCode, targetName})), e.g. "203 Steine von 09 Hellblau werden zu 10 Blau. Fortfahren?". Also let the user choose the replacement colour; removePaletteColor already takes a `replacement` argument.
- StepPlan.tsx:210 "Abschnitt fertig": ask confirm() when the section already has partial progress.

Phase 1 (M): EditJournal, a new file src/core/journal.ts, pure TS with vitest tests.
- Entry types:
  - CellsEntry: struct-of-arrays, not objects. idx: Uint32Array; kind/c1/c2/progress before and after as typed arrays; side maps of sub/line/free clones only for the affected idx. Used for setPieceColor, setCellKind, setFreePieces, replaceColor in a range, and batch shape reset.
  - PaletteRemoveEntry: {prevPalette, removedIndex, target, slots}. `slots` holds only the raw slots that held removedIndex: c1 indices, c2 indices, (subIdx, q) and (freeIdx, k). Undo = shift every index ≥ removedIndex up by 1, then write removedIndex back into those slots, then restore prevPalette. This round-trips exactly (verified in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/value-spec-gaps-3/journal-proto.ts) and its memory grows with the number of stones of that one colour, not the whole project.
  - PaletteEntry {prev, next} for updatePaletteColor, matchAll and add.
- Rules:
  - The stack is LIFO and redo is cleared on every new entry.
  - compute() in useProject.ts clears both stacks. Optional extra: keep the previous packMosaic plus palette as one "Neuberechnung rückgängig" entry, stored in IndexedDB under 'mosaic-prev' so it is not held in RAM.
  - Cap by bytes (~32 MB) and by entries (~200), dropping the oldest.
  - The journal lives in memory only and is cleared when the project is closed; say so in the README.
- useProject exposes undo()/redo()/canUndo/canRedo. Applying an entry calls touchMosaic() (and setPalette for palette entries), so the existing worker stats path recomputes totals. No count or geometry is derived from the journal itself.
- UI:
  - ↶/↷ buttons in StepPreview, StepPlan and StoneDialog.
  - Ctrl/Cmd+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y, ignored while focus is in an input.
  - StoneDialog re-reads its cell after undo.
- Progress gets its own separate small stack in StepPlan laying mode, with a button "Letzten Tap zurück" (togglePiecePlaced is its own inverse; setRangePlaced stores the previous progress slice as a Uint16Array per section row range).
- Update README.md:152 to describe the new state.

Phase 2 (M): batch editing.
- Viewer gets a "Auswählen" toggle. Only in that mode does a one-finger/mouse drag draw a rectangle instead of panning. The rectangle snaps to whole cells via indexAt and yields a Range {r0, r1, c0, c1}.
- Scope choices: selection, current section (existing sec range), or whole project.
- Actions, each one CellsEntry:
  1. "Farbe A → B" through replaceColor(layout, data, from, to, range). Before applying, show the number of affected stones as a dry run.
  2. "Heller/Dunkler": per source colour in the selection, pick the palette colour with the smallest ΔE among palette colours with L* ≥ L+3 (or ≤ L−3). Only existing palette colours are used. If none qualifies, show "Keine hellere Farbe in der Palette – bitte Farbe hinzufügen" instead of inventing one. Before applying, show the mapping, e.g. "09 → 05 (ΔE 4,1)".
  3. "Form zurücksetzen (ganzer Stein)" through setCellKind FULL. Warn when the selection contains laid stones, because their progress will be cleared (undo restores it).
- Lasso selection and per-piece selection are deferred to a later step.
- Tests:
  - undo/redo round-trip equality of packMosaic after mixed sequences (colour, kind, free, palette remove, range replace).
  - stats.pieces unchanged by colour batches, and per-colour counts sum to the total.
  - memory of a palette-remove entry ≤ 8 bytes × stones of that colour.

kept.title: Material matching ignores stock, silently merges colours and never reports which image colours the owned tiles cannot match (req. 8)
kept.problem: Requirement 8 asks the app to prefer owned colours and to suggest the nearest one when a colour is missing. The ΔE gap is computed and then thrown away (PaletteColor.deltaE is declared but never set). Material.stock is never used in the assignment, so over-use only shows up afterwards as a red minus number. There is no notion of owned versus to-buy, and no list of colours to buy.
